analogue_2050.note: Warmer maritime subtropical-trending conditions.

urban_fact: South Korea’s busiest port and the world’s sixth-largest container port, Busan is squeezed into narrow valleys between mountains and the sea, and served as the country’s de facto wartime capital in 1950-53.
image_caption: Busan Cinema Center and the Centum City skyline at night
image_author: Raja Syazwina RS via Wikimedia Commons
educational_debrief: Cityle combines a curated city profile with modelled climate and urban indicators. Use the values as directional clues for play, not as a research or planning dataset.

name: Daegu
peak_smog_season: Summer basin-trapped heat & spring Asian dust (hwangsa)

analogue_current.note: Inland South Korean monsoon-humid-subtropical basin climate.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter inland basin summer extremes.

urban_fact: Sitting in a mountain-ringed basin that traps heat, Daegu produces South Korea’s most extreme urban summer heat island — locally nicknamed "Daefrica" — after decades as the country’s textile-manufacturing center.
image_caption: Nighttime cityscape of Daegu, South Korea
educational_debrief: Cityle combines a curated city profile with modelled climate and urban indicators. Use the values as directional clues for play, not as a research or planning dataset.

name: Lahore
peak_smog_season: Autumn/winter crop-stubble burning and temperature inversion (Nov–Jan smog season)

analogue_current.note: Shares a hot semi-arid subtropical rainfall regime with a short, intense monsoon peak.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer, drier hot-desert conditions typical of the Indus plains under further aridification.

urban_fact: The Mughal-era Walled City and Lahore Fort anchor a core ringed by colonial cantonment districts that grew along canal and rail lines.
educational_debrief: Lahore was ranked the world’s most polluted city in 2022, and its Walled City and colonial cantonment layers now sit beneath a fast-growing Metrobus and metro network built to serve over 13 million residents.
image_caption: View over Lahore, Pakistan, from the Wazir Khan Mosque

name: Bangalore
peak_smog_season: Winter post-monsoon calm-wind stagnation and vehicular exhaust build-up

analogue_current.note: Warm, moderately elevated tropical savanna rainfall pattern with a pronounced wet season.

analogue_2050.note: Intensified tropical savanna heat and monsoon variability under further warming.

urban_fact: Historic market wards (pētes) sit at the core of a tech-driven sprawl across former lakebeds and IT corridors like Whitefield and Electronic City.
educational_debrief: Bangalore’s ‘Garden City’ lake network has shrunk from roughly 265 interconnected tanks to under 100, and its 2023–24 groundwater crisis shows how IT-driven sprawl can outpace water infrastructure even at a relatively temperate elevation.
image_caption: Bangalore (Bengaluru) skyline, India

name: Chennai
peak_smog_season: Winter post-monsoon calm-wind stagnation and vehicular exhaust build-up

analogue_current.note: Coromandel/east Indian coast dry-summer tropical savanna with a similar northeast-monsoon rainfall skew.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer coastal tropical climate with an intensified northeast monsoon.

urban_fact: Height restrictions near the port’s weather radar, lifted only around 2009, pushed the city to sprawl horizontally along the Coromandel Coast rather than upward.
educational_debrief: Chennai’s 2019 ‘Day Zero’ crisis, when reservoirs ran dry mid-year, showed how a single skewed northeast-monsoon season can threaten water supply for a coastal megacity of nearly nine million.
image_caption: Skyline of Chennai, India

name: Kolkata
peak_smog_season: Winter fog and post-Diwali firecracker/biomass burning smog

analogue_current.note: Ganges-Brahmaputra delta-adjacent tropical savanna with a heavy southwest-monsoon peak.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer, wetter tropical conditions with an intensified summer monsoon.

urban_fact: British India’s former capital retains a dense 19th-century colonial core beside the Maidan, still served by one of Asia’s oldest running tram networks.
educational_debrief: Kolkata’s planned satellite townships east of the historic core, like Salt Lake City and New Town, were built specifically to relieve pressure on one of the world’s most densely populated urban cores.
image_caption: Kolkata's central business district skyline, India

name: Hyderabad
peak_smog_season: Winter inversion and pre-monsoon construction dust

analogue_current.note: Deccan plateau tropical savanna bordering semi-arid, with a similar monsoon-concentrated rainy season.

analogue_2050.note: Hot semi-arid conditions with a shorter, more erratic monsoon.

urban_fact: The Qutb Shahi-era old city around Charminar and Golconda Fort sits on a granite landscape once dotted with 140-plus artificial lakes, including the large Hussain Sagar.
educational_debrief: Hyderabad’s post-1990s HITEC City IT corridor grew on the same granite plateau its Nizam-era rulers once covered with artificial lakes for water storage, layering a tech boom onto centuries-old water infrastructure.
image_caption: High-rise office towers lit up at night in Hyderabad's Hi-Tech City
image_author: Mohammad Anees Qamar via Wikimedia Commons

name: Pune
peak_smog_season: Winter temperature inversion with vehicular and construction particulate build-up

analogue_current.note: Western Deccan Plateau tropical savanna bordering semi-arid, moderated by elevation.

analogue_2050.note: Hot semi-arid climate with a shorter monsoon and hotter pre-monsoon months.

urban_fact: Eighteenth-century Peshwa-era peths form the old city core, while a separate British cantonment built after 1817 created a bifurcated old-town/cantonment layout.
educational_debrief: Pune’s shift from a bifurcated old-town/cantonment layout to a purpose-built tech and auto-manufacturing hub at Hinjawadi, Magarpatta, and Kharadi mirrors Lahore’s own colonial-cantonment urban DNA half a subcontinent away.
image_caption: Skyline of Pune, India, seen from Koregaon Park

name: Varanasi
peak_smog_season: Winter Indo-Gangetic Plain haze and crop-residue burning

analogue_current.note: Ganges-plain humid subtropical climate with a hot, dry pre-monsoon spring.

analogue_2050.note: Intensified pre-monsoon heat and a shorter, heavier monsoon burst.

urban_fact: One of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities, its roughly 88 stepped riverfront ghats line a crescent bend of the Ganges.
educational_debrief: Varanasi’s dense, narrow-laned old-city fabric threads between more than 3,300 religious sites, making conventional street-grid infrastructure and modern flood or heat-response planning unusually difficult to retrofit.
image_caption: Ahilya Ghat on the Ganges river in Varanasi, India

name: Thiruvananthapuram
peak_smog_season: Pre-monsoon haze and coastal humidity trapping of traffic emissions

analogue_current.note: Kerala Arabian Sea coast tropical monsoon climate with a flat, narrow year-round temperature range.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer coastal monsoon conditions with heavier southwest-monsoon downpours.

urban_fact: Built across seven hills near India’s southern tip, the city pairs Technopark, India’s first dedicated IT park, with the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre.
educational_debrief: Thiruvananthapuram’s flat, narrow year-round temperature range — barely 2°C between its warmest and coolest months — is a textbook signature of a low-latitude coastal station shielded from continental extremes.
image_caption: A golden-hour evening street scene in Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum), Kerala, India

name: Mysuru
peak_smog_season: Dry-season agricultural burning and vehicular dust in the pre-monsoon months

analogue_current.note: Deccan-adjacent tropical savanna with a comparable dry-and-wet seasonal split.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer elevated tropical savanna with a longer dry season.

urban_fact: One of the first cities in Asia to undergo formal, board-led planned development after 1903, giving Mysuru a wide-boulevard, heritage-preserved core.
educational_debrief: Mysuru’s early adoption of formal urban planning under the 1903 City Improvement Trust Board left it with an unusually low-density, heritage-preserved core compared to most Indian cities of similar size.
image_caption: Front facade of the Mysore Palace (Amba Vilas) in Mysuru, India

name: Kabul
peak_smog_season: Winter temperature inversion trapped in the Kabul valley, worsened by low-grade coal/wood heating

analogue_current.note: High-elevation cold semi-arid basin climate with cold winters and low year-round precipitation.

analogue_2050.note: Drier, more desert-leaning semi-arid conditions under continued warming.

urban_fact: Ringed closely by mountains including Koh-e Asamai and Sher Darwaza, the city’s footprint is squeezed into a narrow Hindu Kush valley along the Kabul River.
educational_debrief: Kabul’s population grew from roughly 500,000 in 2001 to over 5 million today, layering Soviet-era microrayon blocks and post-2001 gated development onto a mountain-hemmed valley never built for this scale.
image_caption: View over the old city of Kabul, Afghanistan

name: Rajshahi
peak_smog_season: Winter dry-season particulate build-up, easing markedly after recent emissions reductions

analogue_current.note: Ganges-basin humid subtropical climate with a comparable dry-winter, monsoon-summer pattern.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer Gangetic-plain subtropical climate with an intensified summer monsoon.

urban_fact: Known as both the ‘Education City’ and ‘Silk City,’ Rajshahi sits on the north bank of the Padma River, the Bangladeshi channel of the Ganges.
educational_debrief: Rajshahi’s local transit runs mostly on electric and traditional rickshaws rather than a formal transit network, and the city posted one of the steepest air-quality improvements recorded worldwide over a recent two-year span.
image_caption: Street-level urban scene in Rajshahi, Bangladesh

name: Colombo
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Feb–Mar) haze from regional agricultural burning and traffic

analogue_current.note: Equatorial Indian Ocean tropical rainforest with year-round heavy, evenly distributed rainfall.

analogue_2050.note: Intensified equatorial rainfall and heat under continued warming.

urban_fact: Portuguese, Dutch, and British colonial periods each left distinct architecture concentrated in the historic Fort district and Pettah market quarter.
educational_debrief: Colombo’s Beira Lake and international port sit within a few blocks of a colonial core shaped by three successive European powers, a compressed layering of history unusual even among former colonial capitals.
image_caption: Colombo city skyline at night with the Lotus Tower, Sri Lanka

name: Urumqi
peak_smog_season: Winter coal-heating inversion, with December often reaching very unhealthy levels

analogue_current.note: Xinjiang desert-basin cold desert climate with an extreme continental temperature swing.

analogue_2050.note: Even hotter, drier desert-basin conditions under continued warming.

urban_fact: Reputed to be the major city farthest from any ocean on Earth, Urumqi sits between the Gurbantünggüt and Taklamakan deserts at the foot of the Tianshan mountains.
educational_debrief: A Tang-dynasty Silk Road garrison town turned modern oil, gas, and petrochemical hub, Urumqi’s roughly 40°C swing between its coldest and warmest month means is among the most extreme continental temperature ranges in this entire pool.
image_caption: Urumqi's central business district seen from Hong Shan, Xinjiang, China

name: Kashgar
peak_smog_season: Spring regional sandstorms, worst in March, compounded by industrial emissions

analogue_current.note: Tarim Basin oasis cold desert climate at comparable elevation and extreme aridity.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter Central Asian desert-oasis conditions under continued warming.

urban_fact: Among the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities, this Silk Road oasis centers on the Id Kah Mosque, one of China’s largest, and its traditional bazaar.
educational_debrief: Kashgar’s historic old town, still predominantly Uyghur, sits at the western edge of the Taklamakan Desert — a strategic oasis crossroads that linked China to Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe for over a thousand years.
image_caption: Kashgar Old City, Xinjiang, China

name: Bishkek
peak_smog_season: Winter temperature-inversion smog typical of basin-ringed Central Asian capitals

analogue_current.note: Central Asian continental basin climate with a comparable spring-wet, summer-dry pattern.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer, drier semi-arid conditions typical of a warming Central Asian steppe.

urban_fact: Laid out on a strict Soviet-era grid with wide boulevards, the city is threaded by irrigation channels (‘aryks’) that water dense rows of shade trees.
educational_debrief: Bishkek’s aryk-irrigated street trees, a distinctive Soviet-era Central Asian planning signature, depend on Tian Shan snowmelt — Kyrgyzstan’s upstream ‘water tower’ position leaves it less water-stressed than downstream neighbors like Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan.
image_caption: Overview of the main downtown road in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan

name: Tashkent
peak_smog_season: Summer photochemical ozone and winter thermal inversion

analogue_current.note: Same Central Asian dry-summer continental Mediterranean rainfall cycle.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter, drier semi-arid conditions typical of the Kyzylkum desert margin.

urban_fact: Almost entirely rebuilt after a devastating 1966 earthquake into a model Soviet city of wide tree-lined boulevards, fountains, and monuments.
educational_debrief: Tashkent’s post-1966 reconstruction produced Central Asia’s first metro system, and the same Csa climate that makes it a close match for Madrid in this dataset is projected to drift toward hot semi-arid conditions by 2050, just as Madrid’s own is.
image_caption: Skyline of Tashkent, Uzbekistan

name: Astana
peak_smog_season: Winter coal-heating season inversion, with January daily peaks up to 64 µg/m³

analogue_current.note: West Siberian steppe humid continental climate with comparably severe winters.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer-summer continental conditions typical of a warming Ural-steppe transition zone.

urban_fact: A purpose-built capital relocated from Almaty in 1997, its Ishim River divides an older northern quarter from a newer administrative showcase south masterplanned in part by Kisho Kurokawa and Norman Foster.
educational_debrief: The second-coldest national capital in the world after Ulaanbaatar, Astana’s entire modern skyline postdates its 1997 relocation from Almaty — a rare case of a capital city whose built form is almost entirely younger than 30 years.
image_caption: Central downtown Astana looking toward the Ak Orda from the Bayterek tower, Kazakhstan
image_author: Ken and Nyetta via Wikimedia Commons

name: Dushanbe
peak_smog_season: Winter valley temperature inversion with significant day-to-day variability

analogue_current.note: Mountain-basin hot-summer Mediterranean climate with a dry, hot summer season.

analogue_2050.note: Hot semi-arid conditions with a shorter, drier rainy season.

urban_fact: Named for the Persian word for ‘Monday,’ reflecting its origin as a weekly bazaar town, roughly 80% of Dushanbe’s built-up area is confined to a narrow valley floor.
educational_debrief: Dushanbe sits in a high-seismicity zone capable of magnitude 7.5–8 earthquakes, a risk that has directly shaped building codes in a city where four-fifths of the urban footprint is squeezed onto an 18-to-100-kilometer-wide valley floor.
image_caption: Central Dushanbe, Tajikistan

name: Ashgabat
peak_smog_season: Summer Karakum Desert dust storms and heat-driven particulate suspension

analogue_current.note: Karakum Desert-margin cold desert climate with a comparable winter-spring rainfall peak.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter, drier desert conditions typical of the Amu Darya lowlands.

urban_fact: Rebuilt after a catastrophic 1948 earthquake, Ashgabat holds a Guinness World Record for the highest concentration of white marble buildings anywhere.
educational_debrief: Ashgabat’s showcase white-marble core sits between the Karakum Desert and the Köpetdag mountains, entirely dependent on the Soviet-era Karakum Canal for the water that keeps a desert capital of over a million people running.
image_caption: View of Ashgabat, the white-marble capital of Turkmenistan

name: Karaganda
peak_smog_season: Winter coal-mining and heating-season particulate build-up

analogue_current.note: Kazakh Uplands steppe humid continental climate with comparably severe, dry winters.

analogue_2050.note: Slightly warmer continental steppe conditions under further warming.

urban_fact: Founded in 1931 as a coal-mining settlement built from scratch on open steppe, the city still depends on the 1960s Irtysh–Karaganda Canal for water imported over 400 km.
educational_debrief: Karaganda’s water supply travels over 400 kilometers through the Soviet-era Irtysh–Karaganda Canal, a concrete signature of chronic scarcity in a steppe city whose coal-mining economy has contracted to just 8 operating mines from 26 in Soviet times.
image_caption: Winter street scene in Karaganda, Kazakhstan

name: Novosibirsk
peak_smog_season: Winter wood/coal residential heating haze during temperature inversions

analogue_current.note: West Siberian humid continental climate with comparably severe, snowy winters.

analogue_2050.note: Slightly warmer continental summers typical of a warming West Siberian basin.

urban_fact: Founded in 1893 at the Trans-Siberian Railway’s Ob River crossing, the city is now home to Akademgorodok, a dedicated Soviet-era science-city research complex.
educational_debrief: Novosibirsk grew from a single railway river-crossing into Siberia’s largest transport and industrial hub, and its Novosibirsk Metro, opened in 1985, remains the only metro system in Siberia.
image_caption: Novosibirsk skyline in winter, Russia
image_author: Novosibirsk travel on Al-Ashraf via Wikimedia Commons

name: Yekaterinburg
peak_smog_season: Winter inversion with road-transport exhaust as the dominant source (80% of local pollution)

analogue_current.note: Ural-region humid continental climate with a comparable severe-winter, mild-summer profile.

analogue_2050.note: Slightly warmer continental summers typical of a warming Ural-Volga transition zone.

urban_fact: Founded in 1723 as an iron-making center on the Asian side of the Ural Mountains, the city retains a large stock of Constructivist architecture.
educational_debrief: Renamed Sverdlovsk for most of the Soviet period before reverting to Yekaterinburg, the city where the Romanov imperial family was executed in 1918 now traces 80% of its air pollution to road transport rather than the heavy industry that built it.
image_caption: Yekaterinburg skyline seen from the City Pond, Russia

name: Ulan-Ude
peak_smog_season: Winter coal and wood-stove heating smog, persistent through most of the cold season

analogue_current.note: Inner Asian steppe-continental climate with a comparably extreme dry-winter, wet-summer swing.

analogue_2050.note: Slightly warmer continental summers typical of a warming Inner Asian steppe.

urban_fact: Sitting at the confluence of the Selenga and Uda rivers near Lake Baikal, the city is Russia’s principal center of Tibetan Buddhism and home to a 7.7-metre, 42-tonne Lenin head.
educational_debrief: Ulan-Ude sits where the Trans-Siberian Railway meets the branch line toward Ulaanbaatar and Beijing, and its razor-thin annual precipitation — barely a tenth of Colombo’s — comes almost entirely in a single summer wet season.
image_caption: Pedestrian zone on Lenina Street in Ulan-Ude, Russia

name: Vladivostok
peak_smog_season: Winter residential coal and wood heating haze trapped in the harbour basin

analogue_current.note: A comparable monsoon-influenced humid continental Pacific coast climate.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer hot-summer variant of the same coastal East Asian monsoon regime.

urban_fact: Founded in 1860 on the Golden Horn Bay, Vladivostok grew as a hillside-terraced naval port around a formal 1868 street grid, closed to foreigners for most of the Soviet era.
educational_debrief: As the Trans-Siberian Railway's Pacific terminus and home to Russia's Pacific Fleet, Vladivostok stayed a closed military city until 1992, shaping a compact port form distinct from most Siberian sprawl.
image_caption: Waterfront skyline of Vladivostok near Egersheld, Russia

name: Irkutsk
peak_smog_season: Winter coal-heating temperature-inversion smog trapped in the Angara valley

analogue_current.note: A neighbouring Siberian river city sharing the same severe continental cold-winter regime.

analogue_2050.note: A milder continental climate as extreme winter cold retreats under warming.

urban_fact: Founded in 1661 on the Angara River just downstream of Lake Baikal, Irkutsk grew fur-trade and gold-rush wealth into ornate merchant architecture after a rebuilding following an 1879 fire.
educational_debrief: Sitting only 72km from Lake Baikal's outflow, Irkutsk functions as the main gateway to the world's largest freshwater reserve, a proximity that keeps its long-term water outlook unusually secure.
image_caption: Karl Marx Street in central Irkutsk, Russia

name: Khabarovsk
peak_smog_season: Winter coal-heating haze over the Amur-Ussuri confluence bluffs

analogue_current.note: A neighbouring Manchurian city with the same monsoon-influenced continental rhythm.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer hot-summer continental variant as regional heat intensifies.

urban_fact: Founded in 1858 at the strategic confluence of the Amur and Ussuri Rivers, Khabarovsk grew a bluff-top historic core overlooking the wide Amur floodplain.
educational_debrief: Khabarovsk served as administrative capital of the Russian Far East Federal District from 2002 to 2018, a river-confluence outpost turned regional seat of government.
image_caption: View from Lenin Square down Muravyov-Amursky Street in Khabarovsk, Russia

name: Chita
peak_smog_season: Severe winter coal-smoke inversion trapped in the Transbaikal basin

analogue_current.note: A cross-border steppe-adjacent city sharing the same extreme continental winter cold.

analogue_2050.note: A milder version of the same dry continental steppe climate as winters warm.

urban_fact: Founded by Cossacks in 1653, Chita grew into the Transbaikal region’s rail and industrial hub once the Trans-Siberian Railway arrived in the 1890s.
educational_debrief: Chita once received exiled Decembrist revolutionaries after an 1827 uprising, whose presence helped shape several of the small fortress town’s earliest civic institutions.
image_caption: Cityscape of Chita, Zabaykalsky Krai, Russia

name: Barnaul
peak_smog_season: Winter heating-season inversion smog over the Ob-Barnaulka confluence

analogue_current.note: Another West Siberian industrial river city on a near-identical continental cycle.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter Central Asian steppe variant of the same continental warming trend.

urban_fact: Founded in 1730 by the Demidov industrial family, Barnaul grew at the confluence of the Ob and Barnaulka Rivers into the Russian Empire’s principal silver-processing centre.
educational_debrief: Barnaul’s identity as a mining-and-metallurgy hub for the mineral-rich Altai Mountains has persisted from imperial silver production well into its modern industrial base.
image_caption: View of Barnaul, Russia from a hill

name: Tomsk
peak_smog_season: Winter heating and petrochemical-industry haze trapped over the Tom River valley

analogue_current.note: A nearby West Siberian city sharing the same wetter, more evenly-distributed continental cycle.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer Urals-region continental climate as summer heat intensifies.

urban_fact: Founded in 1604 on the Tom River, Tomsk was bypassed by the Trans-Siberian Railway in favour of Novosibirsk, arguably preserving more of its historic wooden-lace merchant core.
educational_debrief: Home to six universities and Siberia’s oldest, Tomsk State University, the city carries an outsized student population that keeps its demographic profile unusually young for the region.
image_caption: View of Tomsk, Russia from the fire-observation tower

name: Riyadh
peak_smog_season: Summer Shamal dust storms and photochemical haze over the Najd plateau

analogue_current.note: A near-identical Gulf-interior hot desert climate with the same extreme summer heat.

analogue_2050.note: An even more extreme desert heat regime pushing toward dangerous summer wet-bulb conditions.

urban_fact: Riyadh dismantled its old defensive walls for a 1953 American-influenced grid, later structured by Doxiadis Associates’ 1972 masterplan of 2×2km superblocks along ring roads.
educational_debrief: Riyadh’s decades of ring-road-driven, car-oriented sprawl trace directly back to a single 1972 masterplan grid, one of the more deliberate top-down urban forms in this dataset.
image_caption: Riyadh's skyline at night, featuring the Kingdom Centre and Al Faisaliyah Tower

name: Baghdad
peak_smog_season: Spring and summer Shamal sandstorms combined with dry-season vehicle exhaust

analogue_current.note: Another Tigris-basin hot desert city sharing the same extreme summer temperature swing.

analogue_2050.note: An even hotter arid Mesopotamian-basin climate with intensified summer extremes.

urban_fact: Founded in 762 CE as the deliberately circular "Round City," Baghdad’s modern form is bisected by the Tigris into the eastern Risafa and western Karkh districts.
educational_debrief: Baghdad’s founding plan modelled pre-Islamic Sasanian circular cities like Gur, placing the palace and mosque at the exact centre of two concentric defensive walls.
image_caption: A view of Baghdad, Iraq from the Medical City building

name: Ankara
peak_smog_season: Winter coal and wood heating inversion trapped on the Anatolian plateau

analogue_current.note: A nearby Anatolian plateau city sharing the same cold semi-arid steppe cycle.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter central Anatolian semi-arid climate with intensified summer heat.

urban_fact: Designated capital in 1923 and planned for 500,000 people, Ankara splits between the historic hilltop citadel quarter of Ulus and the grid-planned republican district of Yenişehir.
educational_debrief: Ankara’s Ulus quarter layers Roman, Byzantine, Seljuk, and Ottoman remains around its citadel, a stark contrast to the deliberately modern grid built for the new republic next door.
image_caption: View over Ankara at night, with Kocatepe Mosque and Atakule tower visible

name: Amman
peak_smog_season: Spring dust storms and summer photochemical haze over the highland basin

analogue_current.note: A neighbouring Jordanian highland city on the same hot semi-arid seasonal cycle.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer, drier semi-arid Levantine climate with intensified summer heat.

urban_fact: Built across an original seven hills that grew to nineteen, Amman’s Roman-era Citadel and amphitheater overlook a downtown repeatedly reshaped by successive refugee waves since 1948.
educational_debrief: Amman’s modern growth owes less to organic expansion than to repeated forced migration — Palestinian, Iraqi, and Syrian arrivals across seven decades reshaped the capital each time.
image_caption: Aerial view of Amman's hillside residential architecture

name: Yangon
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Feb-Apr) agricultural burning haze and pre-monsoon dust

analogue_current.note: A neighbouring Bay of Bengal port city sharing the same intense monsoon-fed tropical cycle.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter tropical monsoon coastal climate with intensified storm-season rainfall.

urban_fact: British colonial administrators laid Yangon out on a formal grid after 1852, with broad boulevards still legible downtown around the gilded Shwedagon Pagoda.
educational_debrief: Yangon reputedly holds the largest surviving stock of colonial-era buildings in Southeast Asia, even after national capital functions abruptly relocated to Naypyidaw in 2005.
image_caption: Panoramic view of Yangon, Myanmar from Sakura Tower

name: Ho Chi Minh City
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Dec-Apr) vehicle exhaust and construction dust under weak winds

analogue_current.note: A Mekong Delta city sharing the same tropical savanna wet-dry rhythm just downstream.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter, wetter tropical climate with intensified downpours.

urban_fact: Originating as the Khmer settlement Prey Nôkôr, the city’s District 1 core still carries a French colonial overlay of grand boulevards atop a dense river-and-canal delta geography.
educational_debrief: A dense secondary canal network historically structured trade and drainage here, and now shapes how floodwater moves through one of Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing megacities.
image_caption: Skyline of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

name: Hanoi
peak_smog_season: Winter (Nov-Feb) crop-residue burning and thermal inversion over the Red River basin

analogue_current.note: A monsoon-influenced humid subtropical climate at a comparable latitude band.

analogue_2050.note: A tropical savanna climate matching the threshold Hanoi’s coldest month is projected to cross.

urban_fact: Founded in 1010 CE as the capital of Đại Việt, Hanoi’s Old Quarter still preserves its historic "36 Streets" layout, each once specialised in a single craft or trade.
educational_debrief: Hanoi’s coldest month currently averages just 0.85°C below the threshold separating Köppen’s temperate and tropical groups — a real, mechanically-grounded case for reclassification, not a rounding artefact, under this dataset’s moderate 2050 warming scenario.
image_caption: Panoramic view of Hanoi, Vietnam from the Lotte Center

name: Hue
peak_smog_season: Autumn typhoon-season humidity spikes and dry-season traffic dust in the old imperial core

analogue_current.note: A neighbouring central Vietnam coastal city sharing the same tropical monsoon rainfall regime.

analogue_2050.note: An intensified tropical monsoon coastal climate with heavier storm-season rainfall.

urban_fact: Imperial capital of unified Vietnam from 1802 to 1945, Hue’s walled Imperial City (Đại Nội) sits on the Perfume River, a UNESCO World Heritage complex distinct from colonial French-planned Hanoi or Saigon.
educational_debrief: Guidebooks sometimes file Hue under a milder subtropical label, but its cited climate data place it firmly in the tropical monsoon group — one so wet that October alone can bring more rain than many temperate cities see in a year.
image_caption: Aerial view of the south bank of Hue, Vietnam
image_author: Lê Huy Hoàng Hải via Wikimedia Commons

name: Chiang Mai
peak_smog_season: Feb-Apr regional crop and forest burning haze trapped in the mountain-ringed valley

analogue_current.note: A neighbouring northern highland city with the same tropical savanna dry-season pattern.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter tropical highland climate with an intensified dry-season burning window.

urban_fact: Founded in 1296 as the new capital of the Lan Na kingdom, Chiang Mai’s historic core remains a nearly perfect 1.6km-square defined by surviving brick walls and a continuous moat.
educational_debrief: Despite its 304m elevation and reputation as a cooler hill-country escape, Chiang Mai’s cited climate data confirm a tropical savanna classification — its coldest month still averages nearly 23°C.
image_caption: Panoramic view of Chiang Mai, Thailand from the top of Doi Suthep Mountain

name: Nakhon Ratchasima
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Nov-Feb) agricultural residue burning across the Khorat Plateau

analogue_current.note: Another Isan-region plateau city sharing the same hot tropical savanna dry-season cycle.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter Khorat Plateau climate with an intensified burning-season dry spell.

urban_fact: Known as "Khorat," the city was fortified in the 17th century with a French-influenced moat-and-bastion system, guarding Ayutthaya’s northeastern frontier.
educational_debrief: Nakhon Ratchasima functions today as the principal gateway city to Thailand’s Isan region, a role its historic frontier-fortress position first established centuries ago.
image_caption: Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) skyline looking north, with Wat Sakae in the distance

name: Phnom Penh
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Dec-Mar) vehicle exhaust and construction dust along the riverfront

analogue_current.note: Cambodia’s own second city, sharing the same tropical savanna wet-dry seasonal rhythm.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter, drier tropical savanna climate with an intensified dry-season window.

urban_fact: Sited at the "Chaktomuk" triple confluence of the Tonlé Sap, Mekong, and Bassac Rivers, Phnom Penh’s French colonial-era grid and boulevards once earned it the nickname "Pearl of Asia."
educational_debrief: The Khmer Rouge forcibly evacuated the entire city in 1975, leaving it a ghost city until reconstruction began after 1979 — a rupture in continuous habitation with few parallels among world capitals.
image_caption: Aerial view of Phnom Penh, Cambodia

name: Vientiane
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Feb-Apr) transboundary crop-burning haze across the Mekong basin

analogue_current.note: A twin city directly across the Mekong, sharing the identical tropical savanna cycle.

analogue_2050.note: Laos’ own second city, with a hotter, more intense dry-season pattern.

urban_fact: Established as capital of the Lan Xang kingdom in 1563, explicitly relocated from Luang Prabang for defence, Vientiane remains one of the least densely built national capitals in mainland Southeast Asia.
educational_debrief: Vientiane sits directly on the Mekong River across from Thailand, and its low-rise, spread-out urban form still reflects a deliberate 16th-century capital-relocation decision rather than organic growth.
image_caption: Vientiane, Laos viewed from the Patuxai Gate

name: Surabaya
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Jun-Sep) port and industrial haze combined with vehicle exhaust

analogue_current.note: Another major Indonesian river-port city on the same tropical savanna wet-dry cycle.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter, more humid tropical delta climate with heavier wet-season downpours.

urban_fact: One of Southeast Asia’s earliest major port cities, Surabaya sits on the Madura Strait at the Brantas River delta, its colonial-era layout still organising the old port district today.
educational_debrief: Surabaya grew into the largest city in the Dutch East Indies during the 18th and 19th centuries as the archipelago’s principal trading hub, a legacy still visible in its port district street pattern.
image_caption: A view of office buildings and dwellings in Surabaya, Indonesia

name: Semarang
peak_smog_season: Dry season (May-Sep) coastal haze and vehicle exhaust over the low-lying old town

analogue_current.note: A neighbouring north Java coastal city sharing the same tropical monsoon rainfall regime.

analogue_2050.note: Another low-lying north Java coastal city facing the same intensifying subsidence-linked flood risk.

urban_fact: Semarang’s well-preserved Dutch colonial old town, "Kota Lama," was built as a pentagonal fortress with five watchtowers protecting the original trading settlement.
educational_debrief: Semarang is one of the most frequently cited real-world examples of coastal land subsidence compounding sea-level flood risk, with recurring tidal flooding locals call "rob."
image_caption: Aerial view of Semarang, Indonesia from the tower of the Grand Mosque

name: Kota Kinabalu
peak_smog_season: Occasional dry-season (Aug-Sep) transboundary Sumatra/Kalimantan peat-fire haze

analogue_current.note: Another Sabah coastal city sharing the identical equatorial rainforest rainfall regime.

analogue_2050.note: A comparable Bornean equatorial coastal climate with intensified rainfall.

urban_fact: Rebuilt after WWII bombing destroyed the earlier settlement of Jesselton, Kota Kinabalu sits on a narrow coastal strip between the Crocker Range and the South China Sea.
educational_debrief: The city only regained its indigenous name in 1968, and now functions as the principal gateway to Mount Kinabalu, Southeast Asia’s tallest peak, roughly 50km inland.
image_caption: Downtown Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia
image_author: Ralff Nestor Nacor via Wikimedia Commons

name: Ipoh
peak_smog_season: Occasional dry-season (Aug-Sep) transboundary haze from regional peat and forest fires

analogue_current.note: A nearby historic tin-mining town sharing the same equatorial rainforest climate.

analogue_2050.note: A comparable Malaysian equatorial coastal-plain climate with intensified rainfall.

urban_fact: Ipoh grew explosively after huge tin deposits were discovered in the surrounding Kinta Valley in the 1880s, producing a decentralised, polycentric urban structure amid limestone karst outcrops.
educational_debrief: Ipoh’s Old Town was substantially rebuilt after the Great Fire of 1892, and its scattered layout still traces back to independent mining-camp settlements that only later merged into one city.
image_caption: Cityscape view of Ipoh, Malaysia

name: Kuching
peak_smog_season: Occasional dry-interlude (Jul) transboundary Kalimantan peat-fire haze

analogue_current.note: Another Sarawak coastal city on the same exceptionally wet equatorial rainforest cycle.

analogue_2050.note: A comparable Bornean equatorial rainforest climate straddling the equator itself.

urban_fact: The Sarawak River splits Kuching between the historic Brooke-era "White Rajah" south bank and the newer administrative Astana north bank, a governance arrangement unique in colonial history.
educational_debrief: Kuching’s modern identity dates to 1842, when the English adventurer James Brooke was installed as governor and founded a hereditary personal monarchy that ruled Sarawak until 1946.
image_caption: View of Kuching's central business district skyline from Kenyalang

name: Zamboanga City
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (March-May) agricultural burning haze across the Zamboanga Peninsula

analogue_current.note: A fellow Mindanao city sharing the same typhoon-sheltered tropical monsoon rhythm.

analogue_2050.note: A southern Mindanao city with a shorter dry season, foreshadowing a drift toward year-round rainfall.

urban_fact: Zamboanga's built-up core hugs a narrow coastal strip facing the Basilan Strait, while most of its 1,453 km² municipal area remains forested hinterland.
educational_debrief: Eleven of the Philippines' twelve sardine-canning companies operate in Zamboanga, making a Spanish-founded fort town the unlikely sardine-canning capital of the entire country.
image_caption: Zamboanga City skyline, sea view at sunrise

name: Marrakech
peak_smog_season: Summer Saharan dust intrusions and dry-season particulate buildup

analogue_current.note: Shares a similarly hot, dry semi-arid basin climate at the foot of the Atlas Mountains.

analogue_2050.note: A starker pre-Saharan desert basin, foreshadowing Marrakech's drift toward true hot-desert aridity.

urban_fact: Marrakech's 12th-century red clay ramparts still ring the medina, while an Almoravid-era qanat network historically carried Atlas Mountain water to its gardens.
educational_debrief: Marrakech's 'Red City' walls and khettara water channels are centuries-old engineered adaptations to the same semi-arid Atlas-foothill climate that its cited weather normals confirm today.
image_caption: The Koutoubia Mosque, the iconic 12th-century minaret of Marrakech

name: Fez
peak_smog_season: Winter valley temperature inversions trap smoke over the Fez basin

analogue_current.note: A neighboring Imperial City sharing the same interior Mediterranean climate rhythm just west across the Saïss plain.

analogue_2050.note: A drier pre-Saharan basin foreshadowing Fez's projected drift toward semi-arid conditions.

urban_fact: Fes el-Bali's car-free medina, founded in 789 CE, still follows a street plan laid out for foot and pack-animal traffic over a millennium ago.
educational_debrief: The Chouara Tannery has processed leather using unchanged stone-vat methods since the 11th century, a medieval industrial process still operating at full scale inside a modern city.
image_caption: View of the Fez medina from the Jamai Palace, Morocco

name: Tunis
peak_smog_season: Summer Mediterranean ozone buildup and winter coastal traffic inversion

analogue_current.note: A fellow Tunisian Mediterranean coastal city sharing the same borderline semi-arid/Mediterranean rainfall rhythm.

analogue_2050.note: An interior Tunisian city already fully semi-arid, illustrating the drier climate Tunis is projected to tip into.

urban_fact: Tunis layers three legible eras — the hillside Medina above the Lake of Tunis, the French-era Ville Nouvelle along Avenue Habib Bourguiba, and later 20th-century suburbs.
educational_debrief: Tunis alone generates roughly a third of Tunisia's national GDP and hosts about a third of its registered companies, an economic concentration far beyond its population share.
image_caption: Skyline of Tunis, with the Africa building and Cathedral Saint Vincent de Paul

name: Port Said
peak_smog_season: Autumn agricultural burning haze drifting from the Nile Delta plus spring Khamasin dust

analogue_current.note: A fellow Suez Canal city sharing the same hot desert coastal-transition climate along the waterway.

analogue_2050.note: A Red Sea desert port foreshadowing even hotter, drier canal-corridor conditions.

urban_fact: Founded in 1859 purely to support Suez Canal construction, Port Said still straddles the canal's Mediterranean mouth as a single-purpose infrastructure city.
educational_debrief: Port Said's founding moment was a single pickaxe swing by canal engineer Ferdinand de Lesseps, pinning one of few major cities' exact origin to a single infrastructure groundbreaking.
image_caption: View of Port Said from across the Suez Canal in Port Fouad

name: Suez
peak_smog_season: Year-round refinery and petrochemical emissions intensified by winter inversions

analogue_current.note: A fellow Red Sea desert coast city sharing Suez's extreme aridity and intense summer heat.

analogue_2050.note: A Gulf of Aqaba desert port foreshadowing even more extreme heat at the Red Sea's northern reach.

urban_fact: Suez anchors the canal's southern Red Sea terminus with a refinery-and-pipeline economy, a sharp industrial contrast to Port Said's trade-focused role at the northern end.
educational_debrief: Suez and Port Said were founded together in 1859 as the canal's twin anchor cities, yet diverged sharply: Suez built an oil-refining economy while Port Said built a trading one.
image_caption: Aerial view of the city of Suez and the Suez Canal

name: Kano
peak_smog_season: Winter Harmattan dust haze blowing off the Sahara (Nov-Feb)

analogue_current.note: A neighboring historic Hausa city sharing Kano's savanna climate and Sahel-fringe rainfall pattern.

analogue_2050.note: A true Sahelian semi-arid city just across the border, foreshadowing Kano's projected drift toward drier steppe conditions.

urban_fact: Kano's 14th-century Hausa city walls so impressed colonial administrator Frederick Lugard in 1903 that he called them unlike anything else he'd seen in Africa.
educational_debrief: By 1851 Kano's tanneries reportedly produced 10 million pairs of sandals and 5 million tanned hides annually for trans-Saharan export, a manufacturing identity distinct from administrative Sahelian capitals.
image_caption: Kano cityscape as seen from Dalla Hill

name: Ibadan
peak_smog_season: Dry-season Harmattan haze combined with unpaved-road dust across the metropolis

analogue_current.note: A nearby Yoruba city sharing Ibadan's tropical savanna climate and historic trade-route origins.

analogue_2050.note: A slightly drier interior Yoruba city, foreshadowing a marginally shorter wet season for Ibadan.

urban_fact: Nigeria's largest city by land area at 3,080 km², Ibadan grew from an 1829 Yoruba military encampment into a sprawling, comparatively low-density metropolis.
educational_debrief: Ibadan's enormous 3,080 km² footprint dilutes its population density far below that of far smaller but far denser Lagos, a study in how two Nigerian megacities occupy land so differently.
image_caption: Aerial view of the Alakia area of Ibadan

name: Abuja
peak_smog_season: Dry-season Harmattan dust combined with urban construction and traffic particulates

analogue_current.note: A nearby Nigerian interior city sharing Abuja's savanna climate and elevation band.

analogue_2050.note: A river-confluence city to the south showing a slightly drier, more compressed wet season.

urban_fact: Purpose-built through the 1980s to a master plan radiating from Aso Rock, Abuja formally replaced Lagos as Nigeria's capital on 12 December 1991.
educational_debrief: Abuja was deliberately sited at Nigeria's ethnically-neutral geographic center, hosting the ECOWAS headquarters and an OPEC office as an administrative rather than commercial capital.
image_caption: Abuja's central business district, including the Federal Secretariat

name: Port Harcourt
peak_smog_season: Dry-season gas-flaring haze from surrounding oil facilities intensified by low wind (Dec-Feb)

analogue_current.note: A fellow Niger Delta-adjacent port city sharing Port Harcourt's intense monsoon rainfall regime.

analogue_2050.note: A deeper Niger Delta oil city with an even wetter, more waterlogged annual cycle.

urban_fact: Founded in 1912 to export coal via a purpose-built railway, Port Harcourt shifted decisively to oil after Nigeria's first crude shipment left its port in 1958.
educational_debrief: Port Harcourt's built-up footprint expanded from 6 square miles in 1914 to 140 by the 1980s, tracking its transformation from a colonial export outpost into Nigeria's oil capital.
image_caption: View over Port Harcourt Town, Nigeria

name: Kaduna
peak_smog_season: Winter Harmattan dust combined with textile and steel manufacturing emissions

analogue_current.note: A fellow northern Nigerian interior city sharing Kaduna's savanna climate just east across the plateau.

analogue_2050.note: A far-northern Nigerian city already firmly semi-arid, foreshadowing Kaduna's projected drift toward steppe conditions.

urban_fact: Sited by colonial administrator Frederick Lugard specifically along the Lagos-Kano Railway, Kaduna served as capital of Nigeria's Northern Region from 1917 to 1967.
educational_debrief: Kaduna's economy pivoted from colonial railway logistics to manufacturing — textiles, steel, aluminum, and one of Nigeria's four main oil refineries.
image_caption: The Kaduna Township Stadium roundabout in central Kaduna

name: Kumasi
peak_smog_season: Dry-season Harmattan dust combined with timber-processing and market-traffic emissions

analogue_current.note: A fellow Ghanaian interior city sharing Kumasi's tropical savanna rainfall pattern.

analogue_2050.note: A drier northern Ghanaian savanna city, foreshadowing a more seasonally extreme wet-dry cycle for Kumasi.

urban_fact: Kejetia Market at Kumasi's core is widely cited as West Africa's largest single market, anchoring a city redesigned in 1945 under Maxwell Fry's 'Garden City' plan.
educational_debrief: Compound housing, a traditional Ashanti courtyard form, still makes up 54.9% of Kumasi's residential structures, a holdover against the informal high-rise growth reshaping many African cities.
image_caption: Aerial view of Kumasi, Ashanti Region, Ghana

name: Abidjan
peak_smog_season: Dry-season Harmattan dust intrusions reaching the Gulf of Guinea coast (Dec-Feb)

analogue_current.note: Côte d'Ivoire's drier interior city, sharing Abidjan's savanna-leaning tropical rhythm a step inland from the coast.

analogue_2050.note: A wetter southwestern Ivorian port foreshadowing Abidjan's drift toward a fuller monsoon regime.

urban_fact: Abidjan grew from a small Atchan fishing village on the Ébrié Lagoon after French colonists relocated their capital here in 1896 fleeing a yellow fever outbreak.
educational_debrief: Though Yamoussoukro became Côte d'Ivoire's constitutional capital in 1983, Abidjan retained essentially all real administrative weight — every foreign embassy remains based there.
image_caption: Le Plateau, the central business district of Abidjan

name: Bamako
peak_smog_season: Winter Harmattan dust storms combined with dry-season biomass burning (Nov-Feb)

analogue_current.note: An upstream Niger River city sharing Bamako's Sahel-fringe savanna climate and seasonal flood rhythm.

analogue_2050.note: A true Sahelian semi-arid capital just east, foreshadowing Bamako's projected drift toward steppe conditions.

urban_fact: Bamako grew along the Niger River's floodplain from a 1650s riverside settlement, later expanding across three bridges after becoming French Sudan's capital in 1908.
educational_debrief: Bamako concentrates roughly 70% of Mali's national industrial activity in one metro area, an unusually high single-city economic concentration even by West African standards.
image_caption: Hilltop view over Bamako, the capital and largest city of Mali

name: Lomé
peak_smog_season: Harmattan dust haze arriving via regional transport during the brief dry season (Dec-Jan)

analogue_current.note: A neighboring Gulf of Guinea coastal city sharing Lomé's borderline tropical savanna-monsoon rainfall pattern.

analogue_2050.note: Togo's drier northern interior city, foreshadowing a shorter, more pronounced dry season for coastal Lomé.

urban_fact: An 1880s customs-evasion incentive scheme first drew settlement to Lomé's coastline, an unusual founding driver among West African colonial port cities.
educational_debrief: Lomé's deepwater port, opened in 1904 and expanded with a 1968 free-trade zone, still serves landlocked neighbors as a key export corridor for phosphates, coffee, cocoa, and cotton.
image_caption: Boulevard Circulaire in Lomé's banking district, with the ECOWAS Bank building

name: Cotonou
peak_smog_season: Harmattan dust haze during the brief dry season combined with dense moto-taxi traffic emissions

analogue_current.note: Benin's official political capital just up the coast, sharing Cotonou's coastal Gulf of Guinea climate almost exactly.

analogue_2050.note: Benin's drier interior hub, foreshadowing a more seasonally compressed wet season for coastal Cotonou.

urban_fact: Cotonou is bisected by a canal dug by French colonial administrators in 1855, still structuring the city's layout between Lake Nokoué and the Atlantic.
educational_debrief: Cotonou's city-proper population has plateaued near 679,000 since the 2000s even as its wider metro area kept growing, a downtown core land-constrained between a lagoon and the ocean.
image_caption: Skyline banner of Cotonou, Benin

name: Conakry
peak_smog_season: Dry-season Harmattan dust haze intruding along the Kaloum peninsula (Dec-Feb)

analogue_current.note: A neighboring West African peninsula capital sharing Conakry's extreme monsoon rainfall and coastal mountain backdrop.

analogue_2050.note: An even wetter Upper Guinea coast capital, foreshadowing further intensification of Conakry's already extreme monsoon.

urban_fact: Conakry occupies the narrow 36-kilometer Kaloum Peninsula, a physical constraint that has shaped its growth from roughly 50,000 residents in 1958 to over 3.4 million today.
educational_debrief: Conakry concentrates roughly one-fifth of Guinea's entire national population in a single metro area, an unusually high urban-primacy ratio even by West African standards.
image_caption: A view of Conakry, capital and largest city of Guinea

name: Douala
peak_smog_season: Dry-season port and industrial traffic haze concentrated along the Wouri estuary (Dec-Feb)

analogue_current.note: A fellow Cameroonian coastal city just southwest, sharing Douala's intense equatorial monsoon rainfall.

analogue_2050.note: A foothill city near Mount Cameroon with even heavier rainfall, foreshadowing further wet-season intensification for Douala.

urban_fact: Sited on the Wouri River estuary, Douala briefly served as Cameroon's capital (1940-1946) before developing into the country's economic hub while Yaoundé kept political administration.
educational_debrief: Douala's seaport handles the bulk of Cameroon's — and much of the wider CEMAC region's — oil, cocoa, coffee, timber, and metals exports, a commercial role distinct from Yaoundé's administrative one.
image_caption: Douala skyline viewed from the Presbyterian Health Complex

name: Yaoundé
peak_smog_season: Dry-season regional haze trapped by the city's seven-hills topography (Dec-Feb)

analogue_current.note: A fellow Cameroonian highland city to the northwest, sharing Yaoundé's cooler, elevation-moderated tropical climate.

analogue_2050.note: Another Cameroonian highland city with a slightly drier profile, foreshadowing a marginally shorter wet season for Yaoundé.

urban_fact: Nicknamed 'La Ville aux Sept Collines' (City of Seven Hills) for its markedly hilly topography, Yaoundé has served as Cameroon's political capital continuously since 1960.
educational_debrief: At 726 meters elevation, Yaoundé runs roughly 3°C cooler on average than lowland Douala just 130 miles away, a direct demonstration of how altitude reshapes a tropical climate.
image_caption: A view over Yaoundé, the capital of Cameroon

name: Libreville
peak_smog_season: Brief dry-season (Jun-Aug) haze from regional biomass burning further inland

analogue_current.note: Gabon's oil-industry coastal city to the south, sharing Libreville's equatorial rainforest-fringe climate almost exactly.

analogue_2050.note: A neighboring equatorial Congolese coast city with a fuller monsoon character, foreshadowing Libreville's drift away from a true no-dry-season climate.

urban_fact: Founded in 1849 as a settlement for slaves liberated from the intercepted ship L'Elizia, Libreville later served as capital of French Equatorial Africa from 1888 to 1904.
educational_debrief: Libreville's Nkok Special Economic Zone processes timber for export while the Owendo port handles more than five million tonnes of cargo annually.
image_caption: Aerial night view of downtown Libreville, Gabon

name: Bangui
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Dec-Feb) biomass burning haze along the Ubangi River basin

analogue_current.note: A fellow Central African Republic interior city sharing Bangui's tropical savanna rainfall pattern.

analogue_2050.note: A downstream Congo Basin capital with a fuller monsoon character, foreshadowing wetter conditions for Bangui.

urban_fact: Established in 1889 precisely where Ubangi River rapids blocked further upriver navigation, Bangui's location is dictated by a single navigational chokepoint.
educational_debrief: Bangui's old town retains its original colonial-era boulevards radiating from a central market, a street plan largely unchanged since the city's founding as a river-trade outpost.
image_caption: Aerial view of the Bangui city centre near the PK0 roundabout, with the Oubangui River in the background

name: Lubumbashi
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (May-Sep) mining-dust haze across the Katanga plateau

analogue_current.note: A fellow Katanga copper-belt city sharing Lubumbashi's high-plateau, dry-winter subtropical climate.

analogue_2050.note: A Zambian Copperbelt city just across the border, sharing the same mining-region climate trajectory.

urban_fact: Founded in 1910 as Élisabethville beside the Étoile du Congo copper mine, Lubumbashi's colonial layout still visibly segregates its historic European and African quarters.
educational_debrief: The wider Katanga/Lualaba mining region around Lubumbashi produces more than 3% of the world's copper and roughly half its cobalt, one of the most strategically significant mining regions on Earth.
image_caption: Downtown Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with Hôtel Belle visible at left

name: Addis Ababa
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Nov-Feb) vehicle exhaust trapped by highland temperature inversions

analogue_current.note: A fellow high-elevation Horn of Africa capital sharing Addis Ababa's cool, stable subtropical highland climate.

analogue_2050.note: A lower-elevation Great Lakes highland capital, illustrating the warmer climate Addis Ababa's elevation buffer largely protects it from.

urban_fact: Founded in 1886 as a katama, or royal military camp, Addis Ababa's historic sefer neighborhoods still mirror an army's marching-camp organization.
educational_debrief: As the fourth-highest capital city in the world at 2,355 meters, elevation is the direct cause of a markedly cooler climate relative to every lowland city in this collection.
image_caption: Urban cityscape view of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, near the Kirkos district

name: Kampala
peak_smog_season: Dry-season traffic exhaust and unpaved-road dust across the two annual dry spells (Dec-Feb & Jun-Aug)

analogue_current.note: Equatorial Congo Basin rainforest climate with a similarly narrow, near-constant temperature band.

analogue_2050.note: East African Rift lakeside city with a comparably intensifying, more sharply bimodal dry season.

urban_fact: Kampala spreads across a series of low hills once separated by swamp-filled valleys, its precolonial Buganda-kingdom pattern of hilltop settlements still visible beneath 20th-century expansion.
educational_debrief: Kampala's formal city boundary covers barely 189 km², yet its Greater Metropolitan Area sprawls far beyond it into largely unplanned peri-urban growth -- a mismatch between administrative and lived city size common across fast-growing African capitals.
image_caption: The Kampala skyline across a railyard, Uganda

name: Kigali
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Jun-Sep) traffic exhaust and dust accumulation across the hilltop city

analogue_current.note: East African highland plateau climate with a comparably mild, stable temperature band.

analogue_2050.note: Southern African highland plateau trending toward a more pronounced dry season.

urban_fact: Kigali spans a dramatic ridge-and-valley terrain swinging from 1,300m valley floors to 2,071m hilltops within city limits, its CBD still centred on Nyarugenge Hill, the German colonial post founded there in 1907.
educational_debrief: Rwanda's 2013 masterplan aims to remake Kigali into a 'decentralised modern city by 2040,' and the government's car-free days and plastic-bag ban have already made it a regional reference case for enforced urban order.
image_caption: The skyline of central Kigali, Rwanda

name: Kisumu
peak_smog_season: Dry-season lakeside dust and diesel matatu exhaust near the port and rail yards (Jun-Sep)

analogue_current.note: Same Lake Victoria basin climate on the southern shore.

analogue_2050.note: Lake Victoria outlet city with a comparably stable equatorial rainforest regime.

urban_fact: Kisumu grew explicitly as a 1901 colonial rail terminus on Lake Victoria's Winam Gulf, briefly renamed 'Port Florence,' its triple-mode lake-port, rail, and air hub role still visible in its waterfront-oriented layout.
educational_debrief: As the Uganda Railway's original Lake Victoria terminus, Kisumu's economy and street pattern remain organized around the lakefront port and rail yards a century after they made it East Africa's key inland transshipment hub.
image_caption: Aerial view of Kisumu city, Kenya

name: Mombasa
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Jan-Mar) port traffic exhaust and dust trapped by coastal onshore breezes

analogue_current.note: Swahili-coast Indian Ocean savanna twin with an almost identical seasonal rhythm.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer Indian Ocean coastal conditions under more intense heat.

urban_fact: Centred on Mombasa Island between Port Reitz and Tudor Creek, the city preserves a deep Swahili-coast architectural layer -- the Mnara mosque dates to roughly 1300 CE -- beneath British-era port infrastructure.
educational_debrief: As sea terminus of the Uganda Railway from 1896 and former capital of the British East Africa Protectorate, Mombasa has functioned as East Africa's primary port gateway for well over a century.
image_caption: Aerial view of the Mombasa city skyline from the old town, Kenya

name: Dar es Salaam
peak_smog_season: Dry season (Jun-Sep) diesel bus and truck exhaust concentrated along the port corridor

analogue_current.note: Same-country Indian Ocean coastal savanna twin.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer Indian Ocean coastal savanna as the dry season intensifies.

urban_fact: Founded in 1862 by Sultan Majid bin Said, Dar es Salaam remained Tanganyika and then Tanzania's capital until the seat of government moved to Dodoma in 1974, yet it still handles roughly 90% of the country's cargo.
educational_debrief: More than three-quarters of Dar es Salaam's residents live in informal settlements, a scale that drove the city to open East Africa's first full Bus Rapid Transit line in 2016 as a deliberate structuring intervention.
image_caption: Dar es Salaam skyline from the sea, showing the Tanzania Ports Authority and PSPF Twin Towers

name: Khartoum
peak_smog_season: Pre-monsoon haboob dust storms (Apr-Jun) and dry-season vehicle exhaust trapped over the Nile confluence

analogue_current.note: Sahelian hot desert capital with a comparably extreme, near-rainless annual profile.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter Sahelian desert-savanna boundary as extreme heat intensifies.

urban_fact: Khartoum sits at the confluence of the Blue and White Nile, its metropolitan area actually three linked cities -- Khartoum, Khartoum North (Bahri), and Omdurman -- split by the two rivers and rebuilt after 1898 on a plan said to resemble the Union Jack.
educational_debrief: Between 2023 and 2025, Sudan's civil war caused extensive combat and destruction across Khartoum, a severe and very recent disruption that should temper confidence in any post-2023 'current state' reading of the city.
image_caption: Skyline of Khartoum, Sudan, viewed toward Tuti Island with the Ash-Shahid mosque

name: Maputo
peak_smog_season: Dry season (May-Sep) vehicle exhaust and dust haze along the harbour and Baixa grid

analogue_current.note: Same-country Indian Ocean coastal savanna twin.

analogue_2050.note: Dry semi-arid Madagascar coast, a directional fit for the projected drying trend.

urban_fact: Maputo grew from an 1781 Portuguese fort into a major port by the late 19th century, its planned Baixa grid of square colonial blocks sited on Maputo Bay near four river estuaries, contrasting sharply with its unplanned periphery.
educational_debrief: Mozambique's capital since 1975 independence, Maputo pairs a well-preserved Portuguese-colonial grid downtown with vast unplanned peripheral growth -- a contrast frequently cited in the city's own urban-planning literature.
image_caption: View of the Maputo skyline, Mozambique, seen from Katembe

name: Lusaka
peak_smog_season: Dry season (May-Oct) biomass-burning haze combined with unpaved-road dust

analogue_current.note: Same-country Central Zambian plateau twin.

analogue_2050.note: Transitional highland climate trending warmer toward a savanna profile.

urban_fact: Lusaka began in 1905 as a railway watering stop, then was deliberately designated Northern Rhodesia's colonial capital in 1929 and laid out with a deliberately oversized footprint intended to allow internal infill growth.
educational_debrief: 1930s town planners including Stanley Adshead gave Lusaka racially segregated residential zones and generous open space for later infill, a textbook colonial-planned-capital layout still legible in today's street pattern.
image_caption: Lusaka, the capital city of Zambia

name: Ndola
peak_smog_season: Dry season (May-Sep) industrial refinery haze combined with regional biomass-burning smoke

analogue_current.note: Copperbelt neighbour with a near-identical climate.

analogue_2050.note: Copperbelt-adjacent city trending warmer within the same subtropical class.

urban_fact: Founded in 1904 as a trading post, Ndola became the Copperbelt's industrial hub once the Rhodesia Railways line reached it in 1907, its economy centred on copper refining and logistics rather than the mining itself.
educational_debrief: Unlike neighbouring Copperbelt towns such as Kitwe and Luanshya, which centre on the mine pits themselves, Ndola specializes in copper refining, limestone processing, and petroleum operations -- the province's processing and logistics hub.
image_caption: Streets of Ndola, Zambia

name: Harare
peak_smog_season: Winter (Jun-Aug) highveld temperature inversion trapping vehicle exhaust and wood smoke

analogue_current.note: Zimbabwean highveld subtropical-highland twin.

analogue_2050.note: Highveld city trending toward a hotter subtropical summer.

urban_fact: Established in 1890 on a high plateau, Harare retains a low-density, car-oriented character with alternating streets deliberately planted in colonial-era jacaranda and flamboyant trees, blooming lilac and red each October-November.
educational_debrief: Harare's government district, the Causeway area, began as a drained low-lying stream-bank zone -- part of the original 1890 settlement's concentration along drained ground before the city's now-famous low-density sprawl took hold.
image_caption: The central zone skyline of Harare, Zimbabwe

name: Bulawayo
peak_smog_season: Dry season (May-Sep) industrial haze and dust from the surrounding semi-arid veld

analogue_current.note: Southern Zimbabwe semi-arid twin.

analogue_2050.note: Free State semi-arid city trending toward a fully arid regime.

urban_fact: Bulawayo's CBD streets are unusually wide, deliberately designed to let ox-drawn wagons make a full turn when the town was laid out as Zimbabwe's principal industrial and rail-network hub.
educational_debrief: Since around 1992 Bulawayo has deliberately repositioned itself as a 'heritage city,' foregrounding Victorian-era architecture preservation and railway-museum restoration as an economic strategy distinct from its industrial past.
image_caption: Fife Street in Bulawayo's central business district, Zimbabwe, viewed from Pioneer House
image_author: Prince Phumulani Nyoni via Wikimedia Commons

name: Gaborone
peak_smog_season: Dry winter (May-Aug) dust from the surrounding Kalahari fringe and vehicle exhaust

analogue_current.note: Same-country hot semi-arid twin.

analogue_2050.note: Semi-arid Northern Cape city trending toward a fully arid regime.

urban_fact: A purpose-built post-independence capital planned under Garden City principles with extensive pedestrian walkways, Gaborone grew from just 3,855 residents in 1964 to over 246,000 by 2022, among the fastest-growing cities in the world over that span.
educational_debrief: Gaborone's water supply depends entirely on the single Gaborone Dam reservoir, which also serves the nearby town of Lobatse -- a structural single-point-of-dependency risk central to the city's water-stress outlook.
image_caption: Skyline of Gaborone, the capital city of Botswana

name: Windhoek
peak_smog_season: Dry-season dust events (Jun-Sep) intensified by the surrounding semi-arid plateau terrain

analogue_current.note: Northern Cape hot semi-arid twin.

analogue_2050.note: Sahelian hot desert-semi-arid city, a directional fit for full aridification.

urban_fact: Windhoek grew at a hot spring known to local pastoral communities, refounded by German colonial forces in 1890, and its physical expansion is genuinely constrained by rocky, mountainous terrain on three sides, funnelling growth mainly north toward Brakwater.
educational_debrief: Windhoek opened the world's first potable-reuse facility in 1958, directly treating sewage back into drinking water -- a landmark adaptation to its arid plateau setting that remains a global reference case in water engineering today.
image_caption: The skyline of Windhoek, Namibia, with the Khomas Hochland mountains and Christuskirche in the background

name: Antananarivo
peak_smog_season: Dry season (May-Sep) traffic exhaust trapped by the surrounding ridge topography

analogue_current.note: Same-country highland subtropical twin.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer Madagascar location, a directional fit for continued warming.

urban_fact: Antananarivo is built across three converging ridges topped by the former Merina royal palace, a hierarchical settlement pattern where nobility once occupied the highest ground nearest the palace.
educational_debrief: French colonial engineers bored tunnels through two of the city's largest hills to connect districts, while the lower town expanded outward from the ridges into the surrounding rice-paddy valleys via new boulevards.
image_caption: Lake Anosy in central Antananarivo, the capital of Madagascar

name: Durban
peak_smog_season: Winter (Jun-Aug) coastal temperature inversion trapping port and industrial emissions

analogue_current.note: Nearby KwaZulu-Natal humid-subtropical twin.

analogue_2050.note: South African coast with a comparable warming subtropical regime.

urban_fact: The busiest port city in sub-Saharan Africa, Durban's metro area -- governed since 1994 as the eThekwini Municipality -- formed by merging over 120 formerly independent towns and suburbs, a direct structural response to apartheid-era spatial fragmentation.
educational_debrief: Founded from an 1824 English trading post at Port Natal and renamed in 1835 after Cape governor Sir Benjamin D'Urban, the metro's urban form still carries visible apartheid-era spatial-planning legacies today.
image_caption: The downtown city centre of Durban, South Africa

name: Bloemfontein
peak_smog_season: Winter (Jun-Aug) highveld temperature inversion trapping vehicle and coal-smoke haze

analogue_current.note: Kalahari-fringe semi-arid twin with comparably cool, dry winters.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer semi-arid platinum-belt city, a directional fit for the projected heating.

urban_fact: South Africa's judicial capital, Bloemfontein hosts the Supreme Court of Appeal as part of a constitutional compromise splitting the country's three capitals -- alongside executive Pretoria and legislative Cape Town.
educational_debrief: Established in 1846 as a British Army fort, Bloemfontein served as capital of the independent Orange Free State from 1854 to 1902 before the 1910 Union of South Africa formalised its present judicial-capital role.
image_caption: Bloemfontein CBD skyline, South Africa

name: Blantyre
peak_smog_season: Dry season (May-Sep) biomass-burning haze drifting across the Shire Highlands

analogue_current.note: Same-country nearby highland savanna twin.

analogue_2050.note: Northern Malawi highland retaining the same savanna class with more margin.

urban_fact: Founded in 1876 through Church of Scotland missionary work in the Shire Highlands, Blantyre's topography spans nine distinct watershed catchment areas across numerous hills, a specific hydrological fact that shaped its development pattern.
educational_debrief: Malawi's commercial and industrial centre traces its role back to the colonial-era ivory trade, making Blantyre one of the more distinctly missionary-founded cities in the region rather than a purely administrative or trading-post capital.
image_caption: Blantyre city center at Chayamba Building, facing Mount Soche Hotel, Malawi

name: Milan
peak_smog_season: Winter (Nov-Feb) Po Valley thermal inversion trapping regional industrial and traffic haze

analogue_current.note: Po Valley humid-subtropical twin.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter Po Valley humid-subtropical conditions.

urban_fact: Milan's historic centre still traces a concentric ring layout following the Navigli, an ancient network of navigable canals now mostly covered, itself following an earlier Celtic sanctuary site with an astronomical alignment.
educational_debrief: Leonardo da Vinci personally worked on enhancing the Navigli canal system during the Sforza-era Renaissance, one of the more specific, verifiable urban-engineering facts tied to a named historical figure anywhere in the pool.
image_caption: Milan skyline seen from the roof of the Duomo, Italy

name: Hamburg
peak_smog_season: Winter (Dec-Feb) North Sea coastal haze and residential wood-heating smoke

analogue_current.note: North German oceanic near-identical twin.

analogue_2050.note: Oceanic climate trending toward a warmer, more transitional regime.

urban_fact: Hamburg developed as a medieval Hanseatic League port on the Elbe estuary; its 19th-century Speicherstadt brick-warehouse district still stands as a UNESCO-listed exemplar of that port-city architecture.
educational_debrief: Roughly 2,500 bridges thread Hamburg's rivers and canals -- more than Venice, Amsterdam, and London combined -- and its recent HafenCity development converts former working-port docklands into new urban fabric, continuing a pattern set by post-WWII reconstruction.
image_caption: Hamburg skyline over the Außenalster lake, Germany

name: Munich
peak_smog_season: Winter (Dec-Feb) Alpine foreland temperature inversion trapping road-traffic emissions

analogue_current.note: Alpine foothill oceanic near-identical twin.

analogue_2050.note: Oceanic climate bordering continental with a warmer summer.

urban_fact: Munich was founded around 1158 by Henry the Lion specifically to control the regional salt trade via a toll bridge near today's Ludwigsbrücke, a direct economic rather than defensive founding motive.
educational_debrief: Post-WWII reconstruction deliberately preserved Munich's pre-war street grid even while rebuilding damaged structures, and the city subsequently became a major corporate hub, headquarters to BMW, Siemens, Allianz, and Munich Re.
image_caption: Munich skyline with the Frauenkirche and New Town Hall, seen from St. Peter Church, Germany

name: Marseille
peak_smog_season: Summer (Jun-Aug) photochemical ozone intensified by the Mistral's dry, dust-laden winds

analogue_current.note: French Riviera Mediterranean near-identical twin.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter, drier Mediterranean island climate.

urban_fact: Founded circa 600 BC by Greek colonists from Phocaea, Marseille is France's oldest city by a wide margin, its historic Vieux-Port functioning as a working Mediterranean trading harbour continuously since that founding.
educational_debrief: Modern renewal concentrates in the Euroméditerranée district, a large-scale waterfront redevelopment layered onto former industrial port land -- directly comparable in function, if not form, to Hamburg's HafenCity elsewhere in this pool.
image_caption: Marseille old port (Vieux-Port) seen from Notre-Dame de la Garde, France

name: Amsterdam
peak_smog_season: Spring/summer (Apr-Aug) North Sea onshore haze mixed with cross-border industrial transport

analogue_current.note: Virtually identical Dutch oceanic twin.

analogue_2050.note: Low Countries oceanic climate, slightly warmer.

urban_fact: Amsterdam began as a literal dam on the Amstel River, with organised land reclamation already underway by the late 10th century -- the city's entire existence is a direct engineering response to sitting below sea level.
educational_debrief: The concentric Grachtengordel canal ring -- Herengracht, Keizersgracht, Prinsengracht -- was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2010, a rare case of a still-functioning residential and commercial urban plan receiving that designation.
image_caption: Aerial view of the Amsterdam city center and canal ring, Netherlands

name: Zurich
peak_smog_season: Winter (Dec-Feb) Limmat valley temperature inversion trapping localized traffic haze

analogue_current.note: Fellow Swiss oceanic near-identical twin.

analogue_2050.note: Alpine foreland climate trending toward a warmer summer.

urban_fact: Zurich's Old Town straddles both banks of the Limmat where it exits Lake Zurich, on the site of the Roman settlement of Turicum, and has functioned as Switzerland's primary financial hub since its Reformation-era civic institution-building.
educational_debrief: A principal centre of the Protestant Reformation from 1519 under Huldrych Zwingli, Zurich traces a direct through-line from that era's civic institution-building to its modern identity as home to Switzerland's main stock exchange and major banks.
image_caption: View of Zurich from the Quaibrücke over the Limmat river, Switzerland

name: Manchester
peak_smog_season: Winter temperature inversion trapping traffic emissions in the river valleys

analogue_current.note: Shares Manchester's cool, damp Cfb oceanic seasonal cycle across northern England.

analogue_2050.note: A milder, slightly warmer oceanic climate typical of projected northern-Europe warming.

urban_fact: Britain's first industrial city grew around cotton mills, and its 1894 ship canal let a land-locked centre function as a working seaport.
educational_debrief: Manchester's damp Pennines-edge climate once kept cotton thread from snapping during spinning, fueling the 19th-century boom nicknamed 'Cottonopolis' — the world's first industrialized city.
image_caption: Manchester city centre skyline seen from Alderley Edge, United Kingdom

name: Athens
peak_smog_season: Summer photochemical ozone trapped by the Attica basin's mountain ring

analogue_current.note: A comparable hot, dry-summer Mediterranean seasonal rhythm.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter, drier eastern-Mediterranean climate with intensified summer drought stress.

urban_fact: Ringed by four mountains, the Attica basin traps Athens' congested, non-orthogonal streets between the ancient Acropolis and the modern coast.
educational_debrief: Athens' basin traps summer smog and heat against the surrounding mountains, making the city a long-running European testbed for low-emission zones and odd/even driving restrictions.
image_caption: Skyline and panorama over Athens, Greece, viewed from the Acropolis

name: Porto
peak_smog_season: Winter Atlantic-front stagnation & occasional Saharan dust intrusions

analogue_current.note: A comparably cool, Atlantic-moderated warm-summer Mediterranean climate.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer, more hot-summer Mediterranean regime as Atlantic moderation weakens.

urban_fact: Porto's Ribeira district tumbles down steep granite riverbanks to the Douro gorge, its colorful vertical buildings crossed by six dramatic bridges.
educational_debrief: Porto gave its name to both Portugal and port wine, whose aging lodges cluster across the Douro in Vila Nova de Gaia rather than in the city itself.
image_caption: Panoramic view of Vila Nova de Gaia, the Douro River, and Porto, Portugal, from the Dom Luís I Bridge

name: Warsaw
peak_smog_season: Winter wood/coal residential heating smog under stagnant high pressure

analogue_current.note: Shares the same humid continental seasonal cycle across the North European Plain.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer continental climate foreshadowing Warsaw's more intense summer heat.

urban_fact: Warsaw's UNESCO-listed Old Town is a meticulous post-war reconstruction, rebuilt from paintings and archives after near-total WWII destruction.
educational_debrief: Communist-era planning left Warsaw with wide boulevards and the Soviet-gifted Palace of Culture and Science, still the tallest building in Poland and a persistently contested skyline landmark.
image_caption: Winter sunrise over central Warsaw featuring the Palace of Culture and Science, Poland

name: Kraków
peak_smog_season: Winter coal-heating inversion trapped in the Vistula valley bowl

analogue_current.note: A near-identical humid continental climate in southern Poland.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer continental-to-oceanic transition consistent with milder projected winters.

urban_fact: Kraków's medieval grid survives intact around the vast Rynek Główny square, ringed by the Planty park where the old city walls once stood.
