educational_debrief: Kraków's bowl-shaped valley, ringed by hills, traps winter coal-heating smoke into some of the European Union's worst seasonal air-quality inversions.
image_caption: Panorama of the Vistula River in Kraków with Wawel Hill, Poland

name: Kyiv
peak_smog_season: Winter heating-season particulates & spring agricultural burning

analogue_current.note: A comparable humid continental climate at a similar latitude and continentality.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer, more hot-summer continental climate matching Kyiv's projected summer intensification.

urban_fact: The Dnieper splits Kyiv between a hilly, historic right-bank core and a flat, Soviet-built left bank of large residential microdistricts.
educational_debrief: Kyiv's metro is among the world's deepest, with Arsenalna station reaching roughly 105 metres — a legacy of both the hilly terrain and Cold War civil-defense planning.
image_caption: View of Kyiv from the Saint Sophia Cathedral bell tower, with St. Michael's Golden-Domed Monastery in the distance, Ukraine

name: Lviv
peak_smog_season: Winter residential heating smog under stagnant continental air

analogue_current.note: A near-identical humid continental climate just across the Polish border.

analogue_2050.note: A slightly warmer regional variant of the same humid continental climate.

urban_fact: Lviv's Old Town is one of the most intact medieval-to-Habsburg streetscapes in Europe, spared the destruction that leveled other regional capitals.
educational_debrief: Long passed between Poland, the Habsburg Empire, and the Soviet Union, Lviv's blended Central European architecture set it apart from the rest of Ukraine.
image_caption: Lviv Old Town cityscape, Ukraine

name: Budapest
peak_smog_season: Winter thermal inversion over the Danube basin trapping heating smoke

analogue_current.note: A comparable Pannonian-basin humid subtropical climate with hot summers.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer, more continental hot-summer climate typical of the wider Pannonian basin.

urban_fact: Budapest formed in 1873 by merging hilly Buda and flat, grid-planned Pest across the Danube — a divide still visible in its street pattern today.
educational_debrief: Budapest draws roughly 70 million litres of thermal water daily from 125 springs, one of only three national capitals built directly over active hot springs.
image_caption: Full panoramic skyline of Budapest, Hungary

name: Prague
peak_smog_season: Winter heating-season inversion in the Vltava valley

analogue_current.note: A near-identical oceanic-continental transitional climate in Czechia.

analogue_2050.note: A slightly warmer oceanic climate reflecting Prague's projected summer warming.

urban_fact: Prague's medieval-to-Baroque core survived WWII almost undamaged, filling a deep, winding Vltava valley with one of Europe's most intact cityscapes.
educational_debrief: Ninety-nine watercourses totaling 360 kilometres thread through Prague's metro area, and its 1360s 'Hunger Wall' famine relief-project still traces part of the historic boundary.
image_caption: View from Petřín hill to Hradčany and the Old Town of Prague, Czechia

name: Bratislava
peak_smog_season: Winter cross-border industrial haze & heating-season inversion

analogue_current.note: A comparable Pannonian-basin humid subtropical climate near the Hungarian border.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer, more continental hot-summer Pannonian climate.

urban_fact: The only capital bordering two other countries, Bratislava sits just 50 kilometres from Vienna — the closest pair of national capitals in Europe.
educational_debrief: Petržalka, across the Danube from Bratislava's compact historic core, is one of Central Europe's largest single Communist-era housing developments, housing roughly a quarter of the city.
image_caption: Panorama of Bratislava with St. Martin's Cathedral and the Danube bridges, Slovakia

name: Sofia
peak_smog_season: Winter wood/coal heating trapped by the surrounding mountain basin

analogue_current.note: A comparable mountain-basin continental climate in the Balkan interior.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer Bulgarian climate trending toward a more subtropical summer regime.

urban_fact: Sofia sits in a mountain-ringed valley without a major river, one of few European capitals with no defining waterway running through it.
educational_debrief: Forty-nine mineral and thermal springs have shaped Sofia's public bath culture since its days as the Roman city of Serdica, still visible in the modern streetscape.
image_caption: 360-degree panoramic view from a building in central Sofia, Bulgaria

name: Belgrade
peak_smog_season: Winter lignite power-plant haze & heating-season inversion

analogue_current.note: A comparable hot-summer Danube-basin climate in southeastern Europe.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer inland Balkan climate with intensified summer heat.

urban_fact: Belgrade sits directly at the confluence of the Sava and Danube, a strategic chokepoint fought over 115 times across recorded history.
educational_debrief: Kalemegdan Fortress crowns the bluff above Belgrade's river confluence, while socialist-era Novi Beograd spreads across a flatter, grid-planned left bank.
image_caption: The confluence of the Sava into the Danube at Belgrade, viewed from Kalemegdan

name: Chișinău
peak_smog_season: Winter heating-season particulate haze under stagnant continental air

analogue_current.note: A comparable humid continental climate in the same regional steppe-forest zone.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer, Black Sea-moderated climate matching Chișinău's projected hot-summer drift.

urban_fact: Chișinău was almost entirely rebuilt after WWII under a single 1947 master plan, producing wide Soviet boulevards instead of an organic old core.
educational_debrief: The architect behind Chișinău's post-war reconstruction, Alexey Shchusev, also designed Lenin's Mausoleum — a direct link between this small capital and Soviet planning history.
image_caption: Triumphal Arch and Nativity Cathedral in central Chișinău, Moldova

name: Nizhny Novgorod
peak_smog_season: Winter industrial haze over the Oka-Volga confluence

analogue_current.note: A near-identical Volga-region humid continental climate.

analogue_2050.note: A comparable, slightly milder Volga-basin climate reflecting projected winter warming.

urban_fact: Nizhny Novgorod splits at the Oka-Volga confluence into a hilltop 'Upper City' anchored by its Kremlin and a flatter industrial 'Lower City.'
educational_debrief: Closed to foreigners as 'Gorky' during the Soviet era for its defense manufacturing, the city remains a major automotive and shipbuilding hub on the Volga.
image_caption: View of the Verkhne-Volzhskaya Embankment from Minin Square, Nizhny Novgorod

name: Helsinki
peak_smog_season: Rare winter stagnation episodes in an otherwise clean Baltic airflow

analogue_current.note: A near-identical cool-summer humid continental Baltic climate.

analogue_2050.note: A milder, more oceanic-leaning climate reflecting Helsinki's projected warming.

urban_fact: Built across a peninsula and 315 islands in the Gulf of Finland, Helsinki has an unusually fragmented, water-interleaved form for a national capital.
educational_debrief: A roughly 10-kilometre green corridor threads from Helsinki's core toward the countryside, part of a Finnish planning tradition of wedges rather than a single ring of parkland.
image_caption: Evangelical Lutheran Cathedral seen from Senate Square, Helsinki, Finland

name: Riga
peak_smog_season: Winter heating-season particulates under stagnant Baltic high pressure

analogue_current.note: A near-identical humid continental Baltic climate.

analogue_2050.note: A milder Baltic-coastal climate reflecting projected winter warming.

urban_fact: Riga sits on the Gulf of Riga at the mouth of the Daugava, its Hanseatic-era Old Town ringed by one of the largest Art Nouveau districts anywhere.
educational_debrief: Riga's historic wealth as a Hanseatic trading port shaped a dense, merchant-guild-driven core distinct from the centrally-planned layouts common elsewhere in the region.
image_caption: Skyline of Riga, Latvia, with the Old Town spires visible

name: Vilnius
peak_smog_season: Winter residential wood-heating haze under stagnant continental air

analogue_current.note: A near-identical humid continental climate just across the Lithuanian-Polish border.

analogue_2050.note: A comparable regional climate with slightly warmer projected summers.

urban_fact: Vilnius's hilly, forested Old Town sits at the confluence of the Vilnia and Neris, one of Northern Europe's largest surviving medieval cores.
educational_debrief: A contested candidate for continental Europe's geographic midpoint sits roughly 26 kilometres north of Vilnius, whose lower overall density reflects extensive Soviet-era peripheral sprawl.
image_caption: Aerial view of Vilnius Old Town, Lithuania

name: Tallinn
peak_smog_season: Occasional winter stagnation; otherwise persistently clean Baltic air

analogue_current.note: A near-identical cool-summer humid continental climate within Estonia.

analogue_2050.note: A comparable Baltic-coastal climate with slightly milder winters.

urban_fact: Tallinn's Old Town splits between hilltop Toompea, the traditional seat of power, and the lower Hanseatic merchant town below.
educational_debrief: Tallinn became the first capital city to offer free public transit to its own residents in 2013, a modern policy contrast to its intact medieval core.
image_caption: Skyline of Estonia's capital Tallinn, September 2025

name: Astrakhan
peak_smog_season: Summer Caspian steppe dust storms & winter heating haze

analogue_current.note: A comparable cold semi-arid steppe climate in the same Caspian lowland region.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter, drier Caspian steppe climate matching Astrakhan's projected aridification.

urban_fact: Built across eleven islands of the Volga Delta near the Caspian Sea, Astrakhan was a former khanate capital and Silk Road-adjacent trade hub.
educational_debrief: Astrakhan's extreme continental-arid swings — summer highs above 40°C against a record winter low of -33.6°C — make it one of Europe's most temperature-volatile cities.
image_caption: Ensemble of the Astrakhan Kremlin viewed from the Volga River

name: Zaragoza
peak_smog_season: Summer heat-driven ozone punctuated by the dry, dusty Cierzo wind

analogue_current.note: A near-identical semi-arid Ebro-basin climate.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter, more arid Iberian climate matching Zaragoza's projected drying trend.

urban_fact: Founded as the Roman colony Caesaraugusta, Zaragoza's historic core still traces its original rectangular grid beneath later Islamic and Mudéjar layers.
educational_debrief: The Ebro valley's mountain-sheltered basin produces the 'Cierzo,' a strong, cold, dry northwesterly wind that is a defining and frequently mythologized local weather feature.
image_caption: Basílica del Pilar and the Ebro River, Zaragoza, Spain

name: San Francisco
peak_smog_season: Late-summer/autumn wildfire-smoke intrusions from regional fires

analogue_current.note: A comparable fog-moderated, cool-summer Mediterranean coastal climate.

analogue_2050.note: A warmer Californian coastal climate as marine-fog moderation weakens.

urban_fact: Perched on a hilly peninsula tip, San Francisco's patchwork of hillside neighborhoods grew around more than 50 named hills rather than one grid.
educational_debrief: Rebuilt rapidly after the 1906 earthquake and fire, San Francisco owes its cool, narrow-range Mediterranean climate to a persistent marine fog layer driven by cold coastal upwelling.
image_caption: The Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco skyline seen from Hawk Hill at blue hour
image_author: Daniel L. Lu via Wikimedia Commons

name: Houston
peak_smog_season: Summer petrochemical-corridor ozone under Gulf Coast heat and humidity

analogue_current.note: A comparable hot, humid Gulf Coast subtropical climate.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter, more humid Gulf Coast climate with intensified tropical moisture.

urban_fact: The largest U.S. city without formal zoning, Houston relies on deed restrictions instead, producing famously sprawling, mixed-use-by-default streets.
educational_debrief: Nine miles of underground tunnels and skywalks let downtown Houston office workers avoid the subtropical summer heat entirely at street level.
image_caption: Skyline of downtown Houston, Texas, viewed from the west over Buffalo Bayou
image_author: David Daniel Turner via Wikimedia Commons

name: Dallas
peak_smog_season: Summer ground-level ozone from traffic under stagnant Sun Belt heat

analogue_current.note: A comparable hot-summer humid subtropical Southern Plains climate.

analogue_2050.note: A hotter, drier Texas climate trending toward the state's semi-arid west.

urban_fact: Lacking a natural harbor or navigable river, Dallas grew instead as a rail and highway crossroads, with four interstates converging in the city.
educational_debrief: Dallas Area Rapid Transit operates one of the most extensive light-rail networks by track mileage in the US, an unusual investment for an otherwise highway-oriented Sun Belt city.
image_caption: Dallas, Texas skyline at dusk
image_author: Matthew T Rader via Wikimedia Commons

name: Seattle
peak_smog_season: Late-summer wildfire smoke drifting in from regional fires

analogue_current.note: Pacific Northwest marine climate with a near-identical dry summer/wet winter cycle.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer, more oceanic Atlantic summers as the dry-summer margin softens.

urban_fact: Seattle sits on a narrow isthmus between Puget Sound and Lake Washington, its early hills literally cut down in 20th-century "regrading" projects.
educational_debrief: Seattle's early 20th-century "regrading" projects literally cut down several hills to ease shipping access, while the recent Amazon-driven office boom reshaped the once-industrial South Lake Union district.
image_caption: Cityscape of Seattle just after sunset, seen from the Columbia Center

name: Minneapolis
peak_smog_season: Summer haze from regional and Canadian wildfire smoke

analogue_current.note: Upper Midwest hot-summer continental climate with cold, snowy winters.

analogue_2050.note: Similar continental regime with markedly hotter, more humid summers.

urban_fact: Minneapolis grew up around Saint Anthony Falls, the Mississippi's only natural waterfall, its street grid threaded today by a Chain of Lakes park system.
educational_debrief: The 2018 "Minneapolis 2040" plan ended citywide single-family-only zoning, one of the first major US cities to do so, building on a flour-milling boom once powered by Saint Anthony Falls.
image_caption: Downtown Minneapolis skyline seen from over Saint Anthony Falls

name: Detroit
peak_smog_season: Winter industrial particulate buildup and summer regional ozone transport

analogue_current.note: Great Lakes industrial humid continental regime with a near-identical seasonal cycle.

analogue_2050.note: Similar continental base climate trending toward hotter, more humid summers.

urban_fact: Detroit's low-density, auto-oriented grid spreads along the Detroit River strait linking Lake St. Clair to Lake Erie.
educational_debrief: By 1920, Detroit's automakers produced roughly half the world's cars; since 2014, public-private partnerships have driven a notable revival of the historic downtown core.
image_caption: Skyline of Detroit, Michigan, viewed from the south riverfront

name: Boston
peak_smog_season: Summer coastal ozone trapped under high pressure and marine haze

analogue_current.note: Northeastern humid continental/subtropical borderline climate, same as Boston today.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer humid subtropical conditions Boston is projected to trend toward.

urban_fact: Boston's inner core sits largely on 19th-century tidal fill; the leveled Trimount hills became landfill for the Back Bay.
educational_debrief: The 1991-2007 "Big Dig" buried an elevated highway and replaced it with the Rose Kennedy Greenway, reconnecting downtown Boston to a waterfront built largely on 19th-century landfill.
image_caption: Boston's Back Bay skyline viewed from Longfellow Bridge
image_author: King of Hearts via Wikimedia Commons

name: Phoenix
peak_smog_season: Summer dust storms (haboobs) and monsoon-driven particulate spikes

analogue_current.note: Sonoran Desert hot desert climate with near-identical seasonal extremes.

analogue_2050.note: Even hotter, drier desert conditions Phoenix is projected to intensify toward.

urban_fact: Phoenix's modern street grid dates to an 1870 townsite relocation, and ancient Hohokam canals it later reused still underlie parts of the modern irrigation system.
educational_debrief: Ancient Hohokam canals, built centuries before European contact, still underlie parts of Phoenix's modern irrigation system beneath a 1970s "urban villages" framework designed to manage sprawl.
image_caption: Panoramic skyline of Phoenix, Arizona

name: Las Vegas
peak_smog_season: Summer dust storms and vehicle-heavy Strip-corridor ozone

analogue_current.note: Southwestern hot desert basin climate with a similarly dry, sunny profile.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter, drier desert basin conditions under intensifying warming.

urban_fact: The Las Vegas Strip's casino resorts sit technically outside city limits in unincorporated Clark County, feeding a sprawling desert grid dependent on Colorado River water.
educational_debrief: The Las Vegas Strip's casino resorts sit technically outside city limits in unincorporated Clark County, a jurisdictional quirk shaping decades of local tax-base and governance debates.
image_caption: The Las Vegas Strip at night, viewed from Resorts World Las Vegas
image_author: King of Hearts via Wikimedia Commons

name: Albuquerque
peak_smog_season: Winter wood-smoke inversions in the Rio Grande valley bowl

analogue_current.note: High-elevation semi-arid basin climate with dry, sunny conditions year-round.

analogue_2050.note: Drier, more desert-like conditions as regional aridification intensifies.

urban_fact: Founded in 1706 astride the Rio Grande, Albuquerque is bisected by the river's cottonwood bosque and bounded east by the pink Sandia Mountains.
educational_debrief: Route 66 first ran through downtown Albuquerque on Fourth Street in 1926 before a 1937 realignment onto Central Avenue, which still anchors the city's commercial spine today.
image_caption: Skyline of downtown Albuquerque, New Mexico

name: Winnipeg
peak_smog_season: Summer transboundary wildfire smoke drifting from prairie fires

analogue_current.note: Canadian Prairie continental climate with an almost identical extreme seasonal swing.

analogue_2050.note: Northern Plains continental regime trending toward hotter summers.

urban_fact: Winnipeg grew at The Forks, the historic confluence of the Red and Assiniboine Rivers, and was incorporated as a city in 1873.
educational_debrief: The Canadian Pacific Railway's 1881 arrival fixed Winnipeg's role as rail gateway to the Canadian West, shaping a north-end/south-end divide still visible in the city today.
image_caption: Winnipeg skyline viewed from the Provencher Bridge, Manitoba, Canada

name: Edmonton
peak_smog_season: Summer wildfire smoke from northern Alberta boreal forest fires

analogue_current.note: Northern Canadian Prairie continental climate with cold, dry winters.

analogue_2050.note: Milder mountain-adjacent continental conditions as winters soften.

urban_fact: Edmonton's North Saskatchewan River valley forms one of North America's largest connected urban park systems, threading through 375 named neighbourhoods.
educational_debrief: Long known as the "Gateway to the North," Edmonton is the logistical hub for Alberta's oil sands, with its former downtown airport site now being redeveloped as the sustainable Blatchford community.
image_caption: Edmonton's downtown business district skyline, seen from 98th Avenue, Alberta, Canada

name: Ottawa
peak_smog_season: Summer humid ozone episodes and transboundary wildfire haze

analogue_current.note: Northeastern humid continental climate with a comparably snowy winter.

analogue_2050.note: Similar continental base climate trending toward hotter summers.

urban_fact: The 1950 Gréber Plan created Ottawa's National Capital Greenbelt ring and laid out the Rideau Canal pathway network still structuring the city today.
educational_debrief: A 2001 municipal amalgamation merged Ottawa's surrounding cities and townships into one unified municipality, building on the Gréber Plan's mid-century reshaping of the capital region.
image_caption: View southward of Parliament Hill and the Rideau Canal from Majors Hill Park, Ottawa, Canada

name: Quebec City
peak_smog_season: Summer regional wildfire smoke and humid-air ozone build-up

analogue_current.note: Hemiboreal northeastern climate with cold, snowy winters and a short mild summer.

analogue_2050.note: Similar continental climate trending toward milder winters.

urban_fact: Quebec City's fortified Upper Town sits atop the Cap-Diamant cliff over the Saint Lawrence, its 1608-founded core the only walled city remaining in the Americas north of Mexico.
educational_debrief: Old Quebec's fortified walls, the only ones remaining in the Americas north of Mexico, ring a historic district that became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
image_caption: The Château Frontenac, the landmark hotel overlooking the old town of Quebec City, Canada

name: Calgary
peak_smog_season: Summer wildfire smoke drifting from British Columbia and Alberta fires

analogue_current.note: High-plains cold semi-arid climate with dry, sunny winters.

analogue_2050.note: Similar high-plains steppe climate trending toward warmer summers.

urban_fact: Calgary sits at the Bow and Elbow Rivers' confluence where foothills meet prairie; the nearby 1914 Turner Valley oil discovery cemented its energy-capital role.
educational_debrief: Calgary's downtown core, rebuilt largely in sandstone after a devastating 1886 fire, still hosts regular winter "chinook" winds that can raise temperatures sharply within hours.
image_caption: Downtown Calgary skyline viewed from the Radisson Heights neighborhood, Alberta, Canada

name: Montreal
peak_smog_season: Summer humid ozone episodes intensified by transboundary wildfire smoke

analogue_current.note: Northeastern humid continental climate with a comparably cold, snowy winter.

analogue_2050.note: Similar continental base climate trending toward hotter, more humid summers.

urban_fact: Montreal is an island city at the Saint Lawrence and Ottawa Rivers' confluence, organized around Mount Royal, with the RESO underground network linking downtown.
educational_debrief: Montreal's RESO, one of the world's largest interconnected underground pedestrian networks, links metro stations, shops, and offices across downtown as a direct adaptation to harsh winters.
image_caption: Skyline of downtown Montreal viewed from Mount Royal, Quebec, Canada

name: San Juan
peak_smog_season: Summer Saharan dust intrusions crossing the Atlantic

analogue_current.note: Caribbean tropical monsoon climate with a comparable wet-season rhythm.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter, wetter tropical conditions under intensifying warming.

urban_fact: Old San Juan's Spanish colonial fortifications, including the seaward bastion of El Morro, once guarded transshipment of colonial-era treasure across the Atlantic.
educational_debrief: La Fortaleza, within San Juan's walled colonial core, is the oldest executive mansion in continuous use anywhere in the Americas, part of a fortification system that once guarded Spanish treasure fleets.
image_caption: Modern skyline of San Juan, Puerto Rico

name: Kingston
peak_smog_season: Winter dry-season Saharan dust transport combined with vehicle exhaust

analogue_current.note: Caribbean tropical savanna climate with a comparable dry-season pattern.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter Caribbean conditions under intensifying warming.

urban_fact: Kingston's harbour, often cited as the world's seventh-largest natural harbour, is sheltered by the long sand spit of the Palisadoes beneath the Blue Mountains.
educational_debrief: Kingston's grid, bounded by North, East, West, and Harbour Streets, was laid out after a 1692 earthquake destroyed the earlier capital, Port Royal, across the sheltering Palisadoes spit.
image_caption: Night scene in New Kingston, the business district of Kingston, Jamaica

name: Santo Domingo
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Dec-Mar) vehicle exhaust buildup under weaker trade winds

analogue_current.note: Caribbean tropical monsoon climate with a similarly warm, humid year-round profile.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter, wetter equatorial-leaning tropical conditions.

urban_fact: Founded in 1496 at the Ozama River's mouth, Santo Domingo's Zona Colonial preserves the Americas' earliest surviving European urban fabric.
educational_debrief: Santo Domingo's Zona Colonial, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1990, anchors the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas at the Ozama River's mouth.
image_caption: View of the Santo Domingo skyline, Dominican Republic

name: Medellín
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Dec-Feb) valley thermal inversions trapping vehicle exhaust

analogue_current.note: Central American tropical highland climate with mild, near-constant temperatures.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer highland-tropical conditions as the dry season intensifies.

urban_fact: Medellín fills the narrow Aburrá Valley high in the Andes, its 2004 Metrocable gondola lines pioneering transit access to steep hillside barrios.
educational_debrief: Medellín's 'library parks' built in historically underserved neighborhoods pair with its pioneering Metrocable gondola system as deliberate strategies to address entrenched social inequality.
image_caption: Aerial view of the city center of Medellín, Colombia

name: Cali
peak_smog_season: Dry-season valley haze intensified by nearby sugarcane field burning

analogue_current.note: Tropical valley climate with a comparable wet-dry seasonal split.

analogue_2050.note: Drier tropical conditions with a more pronounced dry season.

urban_fact: Cali fills the flat Cauca Valley floor between the Cauca River to its east and the Farallones mountains to its west, hosting the 1971 Pan American Games.
educational_debrief: Known as the self-proclaimed "Salsa capital of the world," Cali functions as southwestern Colombia's economic hub, linked to the Pacific port of Buenaventura roughly 100 km away.
image_caption: Downtown skyline of Cali, Colombia

name: Barranquilla
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Dec-Mar) port and traffic emissions under weak wind dispersal

analogue_current.note: Caribbean coastal tropical savanna climate with a comparably sharp dry season.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter tropical conditions under intensifying warming.

urban_fact: Barranquilla grew from a 1629 colonial settlement on the Magdalena River delta, about 7.5 km from the Caribbean, into Colombia's principal river-and-maritime port.
educational_debrief: Barranquilla's pre-Lenten Carnival, a UNESCO-recognized Intangible Cultural Heritage tradition, unfolds in a port city whose planning history Wikipedia itself describes as notably chaotic.
image_caption: View of Barranquilla from the Magdalena River, Colombia

name: Guayaquil
peak_smog_season: Wet-season (Jan-Apr) humidity-trapped vehicle exhaust and port emissions

analogue_current.note: Tropical savanna climate with a comparable wet-season concentration.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter, wetter tropical conditions under intensifying warming.

urban_fact: Guayaquil sits on the Guayas River's west bank near its Pacific outlet; the Malecón 2000 project transformed its historic riverfront into a flagship waterfront-renewal example.
educational_debrief: The Malecón 2000 project comprehensively redeveloped Guayaquil's historic riverfront into a modern public park, widely cited as a flagship waterfront-renewal example across Latin America.
image_caption: Panoramic view of Guayaquil, Ecuador

name: Quito
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Jun-Sep) vehicle exhaust trapped in the narrow Andean valley

analogue_current.note: Equatorial Andean highland climate with a near-identical mild, uniform profile.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer equatorial highland conditions under intensifying warming.

urban_fact: Quito sits in a narrow Andean valley below Pichincha, an active volcano overlooking the city, its historic center among the first UNESCO World Heritage sites inscribed in 1978.
educational_debrief: Quito's historic center, among the least-altered colonial-era old towns in the Americas, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1978, the very first year the list existed.
image_caption: Panoramic view of Quito, Ecuador

name: Arequipa
peak_smog_season: Dry season vehicle exhaust trapped against the Andean foothills

analogue_current.note: High-altitude cold desert climate with a near-identical arid, mild profile.

analogue_2050.note: Even more intensified Atacama-adjacent desert aridity.

urban_fact: Arequipa's historic center, built from white sillar volcanic stone since its 1540 founding, sits in the Chili River valley beneath the near-perfect cone of Misti volcano.
educational_debrief: Arequipa's 332-hectare historic center, built from white sillar volcanic stone in the distinctive "Arequipan School" style, earned UNESCO World Heritage status in 2000.
image_caption: View of Arequipa, Peru

name: Trujillo
peak_smog_season: Dry coastal desert haze intensified by vehicle exhaust near the Pan-American corridor

analogue_current.note: Peruvian coastal desert climate cooled by the same Humboldt Current.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter coastal desert conditions with a weaker Humboldt Current moderating effect.

urban_fact: Trujillo's oval historic core is ringed by Avenida España, built along a 17th-century defensive wall, near Chan Chan, the largest adobe city ever built in the ancient world.
educational_debrief: Nearby Chan Chan, the largest adobe city ever built in the ancient world and capital of the pre-Columbian Chimú civilization, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site outside modern Trujillo.
image_caption: Panoramic view of the city of Trujillo, La Libertad, Peru

name: Iquitos
peak_smog_season: Dry-season low-wind stagnation trapping river-port diesel exhaust

analogue_current.note: Amazon river-port city with a near-identical equatorial rainforest rainfall regime.

analogue_2050.note: Congo Basin equatorial rainforest city facing comparably intensified heat and humidity.

urban_fact: The largest city in the world with no road connection to the rest of its national network, Iquitos is reachable only by river or air, a legacy of the 1880s–1914 rubber boom that briefly imported European architecture into the Amazon.
educational_debrief: Iquitos grew from a few hundred residents to nearly 10,000 during the rubber boom, and today its total isolation from Peru’s road network makes it a rare case of a large modern city entirely dependent on river and air freight.
image_caption: Night skyline of Iquitos on the Amazon River, Peru

name: Juliaca
peak_smog_season: Dry-season unpaved-road dust and high-altitude thermal inversion

analogue_current.note: Neighbouring Lake Titicaca altiplano city sharing the same cold, dry-season-driven highland regime.

analogue_2050.note: Bolivian altiplano mining city trending toward a warmer, drier high-plateau profile.

urban_fact: Nicknamed the "City of Winds" for its exposed setting on the Collao Plateau, Juliaca grew explosively after an 1873 railway link and now serves as the commercial hub supplying the nearby La Rinconada gold-mining settlement.
educational_debrief: Juliaca’s warmest-month average sits just above the 10°C threshold that would otherwise classify it as a polar tundra (ET) climate, making it one of the clearest real-world examples of how a single degree can flip a Köppen classification.
image_caption: Panoramic view of the city of Juliaca, Peru
image_author: Omar Vega Ramos via Wikimedia Commons

name: Cochabamba
peak_smog_season: Dry-season valley-bowl inversion trapping vehicle and brick-kiln emissions

analogue_current.note: Another mild, semi-arid Bolivian valley city with a pronounced dry season.

analogue_2050.note: Bolivian valley capital trending toward deeper dry-season aridity under warming.

urban_fact: Founded in 1571 as Villa de Oropesa to supply Andean mining towns with food, Cochabamba has since 2010 recorded more new construction floor-area than any other Bolivian city, overtaking both Santa Cruz and La Paz.
educational_debrief: The 2000 "Cochabamba Water War," a mass uprising against the privatization of the city’s water utility, remains one of the most cited real-world case studies of urban water-access conflict in Latin America.
image_caption: Panorama of the northern zone of Cochabamba, viewed from the Cristo de la Concordia, Bolivia

name: Potosí
peak_smog_season: Dry-season mineral dust from mining operations and thin-air combustion inefficiency

analogue_current.note: Extreme-altitude Bolivian city sharing the same thin, cold, mining-driven climate.

analogue_2050.note: Extreme-altitude Peruvian mining city where warming is pushing warmest-month means above the highland threshold.

urban_fact: Founded in 1545 after Diego Huallpa’s discovery of silver at Cerro Rico, Potosí’s colonial core follows a strict Spanish grid while Indigenous settlements occupy the mountain flank more organically; mining continues today to depths of 1,150 metres.
educational_debrief: By 1603, silver wealth from Cerro Rico had made Potosí one of the largest cities on Earth; its cited Köppen classification is Cwc, not the polar ET originally guessed, because its warmest month sits just above the 10°C cutoff.
image_caption: Panoramic view of the city of Potosí, Bolivia, with Cerro Rico in the background

name: Santa Cruz de la Sierra
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Aug–Sep) agricultural and forest-clearing fire smoke

analogue_current.note: Bolivian lowland tropical city sharing a comparable monsoon-driven wet-dry cycle.

analogue_2050.note: Brazilian agricultural-frontier boomtown trending toward a hotter, more savanna-like dry season.

urban_fact: Santa Cruz has an unusually clean textbook ring-road layout for a Latin American city of its size: ten concentric ring roads spaced 1–2km apart, crossed by 27 radial avenues, all built beside the Piraí River.
educational_debrief: Once a secondary Bolivian city relocated multiple times after its 1561 founding, Santa Cruz is now the country’s largest and fastest-growing metro, producing roughly a third of national GDP from its lowland tropical setting.
image_caption: Skyline of the northern city-center zone of Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia

name: Montevideo
peak_smog_season: Winter thermal inversion trapping wood-stove smoke along the Río de la Plata coast

analogue_current.note: Río de la Plata estuary city sharing an almost identical humid subtropical seasonal cycle.

analogue_2050.note: Southern Brazilian subtropical city with hotter, more humid summer extremes.

urban_fact: Montevideo’s walled colonial core, Ciudad Vieja, stood fortified until 1829; the city today carries strong art-deco and European architectural influence and is unusually finely subdivided into 8 municipalities and 62 barrios.
educational_debrief: Montevideo’s metro area holds more than half of Uruguay’s entire national population, and Uruguay’s near-fully-renewable electricity grid gives the city one of South America’s lowest carbon footprints per capita.
image_caption: Panoramic view of the Montevideo skyline along the rambla waterfront at dusk, Uruguay

name: Asunción
peak_smog_season: Dry-season agricultural burning haze drifting in from the Chaco

analogue_current.note: Argentine Mesopotamia river city sharing the same hot, humid subtropical rainfall pattern.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer, more humid Paraná River city foreshadowing intensified subtropical heat.

urban_fact: Built across seven hills in classic colonial-town fashion, Asunción’s oldest quarter preserves its original street grid; founded in 1537, it launched more than 67 expeditions that went on to found other South American colonial cities.
educational_debrief: Asunción’s metro area concentrates roughly 70% of Paraguay’s entire national GDP, while the country’s Itaipú-dam-powered electricity grid gives the city an unusually low carbon footprint for its income level.
image_caption: Panoramic skyline of Asunción, the capital of Paraguay

name: Antofagasta
peak_smog_season: Year-round mining and port-loading dust under persistent coastal desert aridity

analogue_current.note: Northern Chilean Humboldt-current desert port with an almost identical cool, rainless coastal climate.

analogue_2050.note: Chile’s northernmost desert city, hotter still under the same hyper-arid coastal regime.

urban_fact: Built on 19th-century saltpeter mining, Antofagasta has since become a strategic copper-export port and, since the 2010s, a hub for lithium extraction from the Atacama’s brine deposits — a three-act mining economy in one city.
educational_debrief: The World Resources Institute projects Chile moving from medium to extremely high water stress by 2040, and few places illustrate that risk more starkly than Antofagasta, a mining metropolis in one of the driest inhabited places on Earth.
image_caption: Panorama of the southern sector skyline of Antofagasta, Chile

name: Curitiba
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Jun–Aug) temperature inversion trapping vehicle exhaust on the plateau

analogue_current.note: Southern Brazilian highland city sharing a comparably mild, humid subtropical plateau climate.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer Paraná state city trending from oceanic-leaning toward a firmer humid-subtropical regime.

urban_fact: Curitiba is the internationally recognized birthplace of modern Bus Rapid Transit, developed under architect-mayor Jaime Lerner’s 1960s–70s master plan; the city still maintains 51.5 square metres of green space per resident.
educational_debrief: UNESCO cited Curitiba’s Trinary Road System as a model for rebuilding Afghan cities, and its exclusive-lane, tube-station bus network proved that a car-free-feeling transit backbone could be built without a subway.
image_caption: Skyline of Curitiba, Paraná, Brazil

name: Recife
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Sep–Dec) coastal haze and sugarcane-harvest burning

analogue_current.note: Neighbouring Nordeste coastal city sharing an almost identical tropical monsoon rainfall regime.

analogue_2050.note: Nordeste coastal city trending toward hotter, more humid monsoon extremes.

urban_fact: Called the "Venice of Brazil," Recife is cut into three islands by the Beberibe and Capibaribe rivers and linked by more than 50 bridges; it briefly served as the capital of 17th-century Dutch colonial Brazil, Mauritsstad, from 1630 to 1654.
educational_debrief: Recife’s low-lying, river-cut island geography that earned it the "Venice of Brazil" nickname is the same geography that now drives some of the most severe urban flood exposure of any city in this batch.
image_caption: Panoramic cityscape of Recife, Pernambuco, Brazil

name: Fortaleza
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Aug–Dec) trade-wind dust with minimal industrial haze

analogue_current.note: Neighbouring Nordeste coastal city with the same distinctive dry-summer tropical rainfall pattern.

analogue_2050.note: Nordeste coastal city where the dry season is trending sharper and longer.

urban_fact: State capital of Ceará, Fortaleza was renamed from the Dutch-built Fort Schoonenborch (1649) after the Portuguese took it in 1726; its Cocó Park, preserving mangrove ecosystems within the metro area, is one of the largest urban parks in Latin America.
educational_debrief: Fortaleza’s rainfall pattern is a textbook dry-summer tropical (As) climate, an uncommon reversal of the far more common wet-summer pattern seen in most tropical cities — its driest months fall in the high-sun season, not the low-sun one.
image_caption: Skyline of Fortaleza, Ceará, Brazil, seen from the sea

name: Belém
peak_smog_season: Dry-season (Aug–Nov) regional deforestation and wildfire smoke drifting from the interior

analogue_current.note: Equatorial Amazon river-mouth city sharing an almost identical constant heat and rainfall profile.

analogue_2050.note: Equatorial African coastal city facing comparably intensified rainforest heat and humidity.

urban_fact: A major Amazon River port roughly 100km upriver from the Atlantic, Belém was founded by the Portuguese in 1616 and today handles aluminum, iron ore, and Brazil-nut exports drawn from across the Amazon basin.
educational_debrief: Belém hosted the UN’s COP30 climate conference in 2025, putting a real Amazon-mouth port city with 3,300mm of annual rainfall directly at the center of global climate diplomacy.
image_caption: Panorama of Praça da República (Republic Square) in downtown Belém, Pará, Brazil

name: Maracaibo
peak_smog_season: Dry-season stagnant heat trapping refinery and vehicle emissions around the lake basin

analogue_current.note: Colombian hot semi-arid city sharing a comparably scorching, seasonally dry lowland climate.

analogue_2050.note: Colombian Caribbean desert-fringe city foreshadowing deeper aridity and heat.

urban_fact: Sitting on the strait linking Lake Maracaibo to the Gulf of Venezuela, Maracaibo is the country’s oil-economic center; the General Rafael Urdaneta Bridge, opened in 1962, ended nearly 380 years of the city’s road isolation from the rest of Venezuela.
educational_debrief: The Lake Maracaibo basin supplies roughly two-thirds of Venezuela’s total petroleum output, making one of South America’s hottest cities also one of its most economically consequential.
image_caption: Panoramic skyline view of Maracaibo, Venezuela

name: Mérida
peak_smog_season: Dry-season valley inversion trapping vehicle exhaust below the cable-car ridgeline

analogue_current.note: Neighbouring Venezuelan Andean city sharing the same mild, tropical highland-valley climate.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer Colombian Andean-border valley city foreshadowing hotter highland conditions.

urban_fact: Venezuela’s highest city, Mérida sits in a Chama River valley below Pico Bolívar, the country’s tallest peak, and hosts what sources describe as the highest and among the longest cable-car systems in the world, climbing toward Pico Espejo.
educational_debrief: Home to the Universidad de los Andes since 1811, Mérida’s tropical-latitude location combined with 1,630m of elevation gives it near-constant, spring-like temperatures year-round — a hallmark of tropical highland climates.
image_caption: Panoramic view of Mérida, Venezuela, seen from the El Morro road

name: Brisbane
peak_smog_season: Summer bushfire smoke events and humid subtropical ozone buildup

analogue_current.note: US Southeast humid subtropical city with a comparably hot, storm-prone coastal climate.

analogue_2050.note: Hotter, more humid Gulf Coast city foreshadowing intensified subtropical extremes.

urban_fact: Brisbane’s CBD sits on a peninsula of the Brisbane River about 15km from Moreton Bay, with the built-up metro sprawling roughly 100km along the floodplain from Caboolture to Beenleigh; it served as General MacArthur’s Pacific command headquarters in WWII.
educational_debrief: Brisbane’s river-floodplain setting that shaped its distinctive sprawling urban form is the same geography behind its well-documented major flood events, making flood risk a structural feature of the city rather than a rare anomaly.
image_caption: Sunrise over the Brisbane River and city skyline, Australia
image_author: Cyron Ray Macey via Wikimedia Commons

name: Canberra
peak_smog_season: Summer bushfire smoke settling into the basin under still, inversion-prone conditions

analogue_current.note: Victorian inland highland city sharing a comparably cool, dry-summer temperate climate.

analogue_2050.note: Queensland highland city foreshadowing a warmer, drier inland-basin future.

urban_fact: An entirely planned capital designed by Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin, Canberra’s land axis runs from Capital Hill through a central basin to the Australian War Memorial — a rare, fully intentional geometric city plan chosen as a compromise between rival Sydney and Melbourne.
educational_debrief: With the Australian Public Service accounting for roughly a quarter of all Canberra jobs, the city’s public-administration-driven economy gives it a notably narrower income spread than Australia’s larger, more diversified metros.
image_caption: Panorama of Canberra, Australia, viewed from the Mount Ainslie Lookout

name: Gold Coast
peak_smog_season: Summer sea-breeze haze and occasional bushfire smoke drifting from the hinterland

analogue_current.note: Neighbouring Queensland coastal tourism region with an almost identical humid subtropical climate.

analogue_2050.note: Hot, humid Gulf Coast tourism city foreshadowing intensified subtropical extremes.

urban_fact: A 60–70km coastal high-rise strip built almost entirely for tourism, the Gold Coast draws nearly 10 million visitors a year accounting for roughly 1 in 4 local jobs, with more than 260km of artificial canals replacing former coastal wetlands.
educational_debrief: Its first high-rise went up in 1960, and major skyscraper construction followed from the 1980s onward, making the Gold Coast one of the world’s clearest examples of a metropolis purpose-built for tourism rather than growing organically around trade or industry.
image_caption: Skyscrapers of Surfers Paradise, Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia

name: Newcastle
peak_smog_season: Winter coal-dust and port-loading particulates under still harbour air

analogue_current.note: Fellow NSW industrial coal-port city with an almost identical humid subtropical coastal climate.

analogue_2050.note: US Southeast coastal port city foreshadowing hotter, more humid conditions.

urban_fact: The world’s largest coal-export port, moving 143 million tonnes in 2022, Newcastle built a 200-year history as an industrial shipping hub at the mouth of the Hunter River before its steelworks closed in 1999 after 84 years and roughly 50,000 workers.
educational_debrief: Founded in 1804 as a secondary-punishment convict settlement named for Newcastle-upon-Tyne, the city’s post-steelworks shift toward services and education is a well-documented case study in deindustrialization and urban reinvention.
image_caption: Aerial photograph of Newcastle, New South Wales, Australia

name: Geelong
peak_smog_season: Winter woodsmoke and light-industrial haze over Corio Bay

analogue_current.note: Fellow Victorian coastal city sharing a comparably cool, temperate oceanic climate.

analogue_2050.note: Inland Victorian city foreshadowing a warmer, drier summer season.

urban_fact: Historically Australia’s major wool-processing and manufacturing port on Corio Bay’s western shore, Geelong earned the nickname "The Pivot" as an 1860s-era shipping and rail hub serving regional Victoria.
educational_debrief: Geelong’s cited Köppen classification is Cfb, not the drier Csb originally guessed for it — its driest three months are only moderately drier than its wettest, a mild seasonal contrast rather than a true dry-summer pattern.
image_caption: Aerial view of Geelong and the Royal Geelong Yacht Club, Victoria, Australia

name: Hobart
peak_smog_season: Winter wood-heater smoke pooling in the Derwent valley on still, cold nights

analogue_current.note: Cool, temperate Southern Hemisphere city sharing a comparably mild, wet oceanic climate.

analogue_2050.note: Tasmania’s second city, slightly warmer and drier under the same oceanic regime.

urban_fact: Hobart’s harbour, built largely on reclaimed land, is described as the world’s second-deepest natural port; founded in 1804 as a British penal colony, its well-preserved Georgian and Victorian convict-built architecture is now a major tourism draw.
educational_debrief: Tasmania’s hydro-powered electricity grid gives Hobart one of the lowest carbon footprints of any Australian capital, while its cool, wet climate makes it Australia’s least heat-exposed capital-class city under this dataset’s own metrics.

name: Wellington
peak_smog_season: Winter calm-morning wood-smoke episodes, rare given the city’s near-constant wind

analogue_current.note: South Island city sharing a comparably cool, windy, temperate oceanic climate.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer, sunnier New Zealand city foreshadowing milder oceanic winters.

urban_fact: Frequently cited as the world’s windiest city by average wind speed, "Windy Wellington" expands along valleys and hillside slopes rather than a single planned grid; the 1855 earthquake permanently raised parts of the waterfront by 2–3 metres.
educational_debrief: Wellington’s GDP per capita runs well above New Zealand’s national average, reflecting how concentrating national-government and finance-sector output into one compact, terrain-constrained capital can outweigh its small population.

name: Christchurch
peak_smog_season: Winter calm-night temperature inversion trapping home-heating woodsmoke on the Canterbury Plains

analogue_current.note: Neighbouring South Island rain-shadow city sharing an almost identical drier temperate climate.

analogue_2050.note: Warmer, drier Marlborough region city foreshadowing deeper rain-shadow aridity.

urban_fact: Christchurch’s central-city grid of streets, squares, and parkland was laid out by 1850, one of the most explicitly planned colonial-era grids in this batch, sitting on flat alluvial-gravel Canterbury Plains fed by an artesian aquifer system.
educational_debrief: Following the 2010–2011 earthquakes, more than 8,000 homes in "residential red zones" were demolished or relocated, with substantial subsequent growth in the purpose-built East Frame redevelopment — a well-documented disaster-recovery urban-form story.
